with test(*[f"datakit._source.Source.{m}" for m in ("__init__", "files", "read", "stream", "groups", "mesh", "grid", "vertical", "coords", "depth", "time_hours", "snapshot")], "datakit._source.source", "datakit._source.derived", "datakit._write.write_field", "datakit._write.provenance", "datakit._write.history", "preprocessing.baroclinic.split", "orcakit.grid_c.vertical_velocity", "datakit._source.Source.point_mask", "datakit._source.Source.point_coords", "orcakit.paths.get"):
    from orcakit import paths as PA
    toml = os.path.join(TMP, "paths.toml")
    with open(toml, "w") as t_: t_.write('one = "~/x"\n')
    saved = os.environ.get("LU_PATHS"); os.environ["LU_PATHS"] = toml
    yes("location read, with ~ expanded", PA.get("one") == os.path.expanduser("~/x"))
    yes("unset location gives a placeholder that names it", "two" in PA.get("two") and "not set" in PA.get("two"))
    if saved is None: del os.environ["LU_PATHS"]
    else: os.environ["LU_PATHS"] = saved
    nz, ny, nx = 3, 12, 16; e3 = np.array([10., 20., 30.]); mesh = os.path.join(TMP, "stage0_mesh.nc")
    tm = np.ones((nz, ny, nx), "i1"); tm[:, 5, 6] = 0
    um = tm*np.roll(tm, -1, axis=2); vm = tm*np.roll(tm, -1, axis=1)
    with netCDF4.Dataset(mesh, "w") as nc:
        for d, s in (("t", 1), ("z", nz), ("y", ny), ("x", nx)): nc.createDimension(d, s)
        nc.createVariable("e3t_0", "f8", ("t", "z"))[:] = e3
        nc.createVariable("e3t_ps", "f8", ("t", "y", "x"))[:] = e3[-1]
        for n_, a in (("tmask", tm), ("umask", um), ("vmask", vm)): nc.createVariable(n_, "i1", ("t", "z", "y", "x"))[:] = a
        for n_ in ("gphit", "glamt", "gphiu", "glamu", "e1t", "e2t", "e1u", "e2u", "e1v", "e2v", "e1f", "e2f"): nc.createVariable(n_, "f8", ("t", "y", "x"))[:] = 1000.
    S = SRC.Source("fake", os.path.join(TMP, "stage0_raw"), [mesh], "fk", 86400.)
    e3u, e3v, u_m, v_m = S.vertical(np.float64)
    yes("masks returned as boolean", u_m.dtype == bool and v_m.dtype == bool)
    ok("e3u is e3t_0 on wet points", (e3u - e3[:, None, None])[:, 1:-2, 1:-2][u_m[:, 1:-2, 1:-2]], 1e-12)
    ok("e3v is e3t_0 on wet points", (e3v - e3[:, None, None])[:, 1:-2, 1:-2][v_m[:, 1:-2, 1:-2]], 1e-12)
    g_ = S.grid(); yes("grid names the boundary and the metrics", g_["boundary"] == "t-fold" and g_["e1u"].shape == (ny, nx) and g_["lat"].shape == (ny, nx))
    yes("mesh reads by name", S.mesh("e3t_0").shape == (nz,))
    try:
        SRC.Source("f", "", [mesh], "f", 1., boundary="closed").vertical(); yes("other boundaries refused", False)
    except NotImplementedError:
        yes("other boundaries refused", True)
    u = 0.1*np.arange(1., nz*ny*nx + 1).reshape(nz, ny, nx)/(nz*ny*nx); u[:, 5, 6] = np.nan
    bt, bc = BC.split(u, e3u, u_m)
    w = e3u*u_m; ok("baroclinic part has zero weighted depth mean", np.nansum(np.nan_to_num(bc)*w, axis=0), 1e-11)
    wet = u_m.all(axis=0); ok("the parts rebuild the field", (bc + bt[None] - u)[:, wet], 1e-12)
    ok("barotropic is the weighted mean, hand value", bt[0, 0] - np.sum(u[:, 0, 0]*e3)/e3.sum(), 1e-12)
    yes("land is NaN in both parts", np.isnan(bc[0, 5, 6]) and np.isnan(bt[5, 6]) and (np.isnan(bc) == ~u_m).all())
    attrs = WR.provenance(source="fake"); yes("provenance has commit, command, date and extras", all(k in attrs for k in ("git_commit", "command", "created", "source")))
    lat, lon = np.zeros((ny, nx)), np.zeros((ny, nx)); dep = np.array([5., 20., 45.]); root = S.root
    for i, date in enumerate(("2015-01-01", "2015-01-02")):
        for var, sign in (("u", 1.), ("v", -1.)):
            p = WR.write_field(root, var, date, sign*(i + 1)*u, lat, lon, 100. + i, "fk", dep, np.float64 if var == "v" else np.float32, attrs)
    yes("path follows the convention", p.endswith(os.path.join("vomecrty", "vomecrty_fk_2015-01-02.nc")) and not glob.glob(p + ".tmp*"))
    with netCDF4.Dataset(p) as nc:
        yes("file convention", nc["vomecrty"].dimensions == ("deptht", "y", "x") and nc["time_counter"].shape == () and np.isnan(nc["vomecrty"]._FillValue) and nc["vomecrty"].filters()["zlib"] and nc["vomecrty"].dtype == np.float64 and nc.source == "fake")
    bt_path = WR.write_field(os.path.join(TMP, "stage0_bt"), "v", "2015-01-01", bt, lat, lon, 100., "fk")
    with netCDF4.Dataset(bt_path) as nc: yes("2D field has no depth", nc["vomecrty"].dimensions == ("y", "x"))
    both = WR.write_field(os.path.join(TMP, "stage0_split"), "v", "2015-01-01", bc, lat, lon, 100., "fk", dep, np.float64, attrs, {"vobtcrty": bt})
    Sp = SRC.derived(os.path.join(TMP, "stage0_split"), S)
    yes("both parts share one file", Sp.files("vbt") == Sp.files("v") == [both])
    with netCDF4.Dataset(both) as nc: yes("barotropic part is 2D, baroclinic 3D, same type", nc["vobtcrty"].dimensions == ("y", "x") and nc["vomecrty"].dimensions == ("deptht", "y", "x") and nc["vobtcrty"].dtype == np.float64)
    ok("barotropic part reads back by common name", np.nan_to_num(Sp.read("vbt")[0] - np.float32(bt)), 1e-6)
    ok("baroclinic part reads back by common name", np.nan_to_num(Sp.read("v", level=None)[0] - np.float32(bc)), 1e-6)
    import _common as CM
    yes("resume accepts the same precision", not CM.incompatible(both, ("vomecrty", "vobtcrty"), np.float64))
    yes("resume refuses another precision", CM.incompatible(both, ("vomecrty", "vobtcrty"), np.float32))
    yes("resume refuses a file with one part", CM.incompatible(p, ("vomecrty", "vobtcrty"), np.float64))
    WV = lambda a, b, m: grid_c.vertical_velocity(a, b, exchange=orca.halo, **m)
    yes("point mask by name", S.point_mask("U").dtype == bool)
    pc = S.point_coords("U"); yes("point coordinates from the mesh", len(pc) == 2 and pc[0].shape == (ny, nx))
    gr = S.grid(); M_ = dict(e3u=e3u, e3v=e3v, umask=np.ones_like(u_m), vmask=np.ones_like(v_m), tmask=np.ones_like(u_m), e1t=gr["e1t"], e2t=gr["e2t"], e1v=gr["e1v"], e2u=gr["e2u"])
    M_["e3u"] = M_["e3v"] = e3[:, None, None]*np.ones((nz, ny, nx))
    w_ = WV(np.full((nz, ny, nx), 0.3), np.full((nz, ny, nx), 0.0), M_)
    ok("uniform flow in a periodic channel has no w", w_[:, 1:, 1:-1], 1e-12)
    jj_ = np.arange(ny)[None, :, None]*np.ones((nz, ny, nx)); w_ = WV(np.zeros((nz, ny, nx)), 1e-3*jj_, M_)
    ok("constant divergence gives w by hand, top of the column", w_[0, 3:-3, 3:-3] + 1e-6*e3[:-1].sum(), 1e-12)
    yes("w is NaN on land", np.isnan(WV(np.zeros((nz, ny, nx)), np.zeros((nz, ny, nx)), {**M_, "tmask": tm.astype(bool)})[0, 5, 6]))
    dep_ = WR.write_field(os.path.join(TMP, "stage0_w"), "w", "2015-01-01", w_, lat, lon, 100., "fk", dep, depth_name="depthw")
    with netCDF4.Dataset(dep_) as nc: yes("w files use W levels", nc["vovecrtz"].dimensions == ("depthw", "y", "x"))
    raw_ = os.path.join(TMP, "raw_hist.nc")
    with netCDF4.Dataset(raw_, "w") as nc: nc.history = "made upstream"
    h1 = WR.provenance("PP1 baroclinic: split", raw_)["history"]
    yes("first step: its line, then the raw file and its own history", h1.splitlines()[0].endswith(" | " + os.path.basename(sys.argv[0]) + " " + " ".join(sys.argv[1:])) and "PP1 baroclinic: split" in h1.splitlines()[0] and h1.splitlines()[1:] == ["source file: raw_hist.nc", "made upstream"])
    mid_ = WR.write_field(os.path.join(TMP, "hist"), "u", "2015-01-01", bt, lat, lon, 100., "fk", attrs=WR.provenance("PP1 baroclinic: split", raw_))
    h2 = WR.provenance("PP4 spatial_filter: low", mid_)["history"].splitlines()
    yes("second step goes on top of the first, newest first", "PP4" in h2[0] and "PP1" in h2[1] and h2[2] == "source file: raw_hist.nc")
    yes("no git commit in history", all("git" not in l for l in h2))
    h3 = WR.provenance("PP7 running: cov", {"u": mid_, "v": raw_})["history"].splitlines()
    yes("two inputs keep both histories, indented", h3[1] == "inputs: u" and h3[2].startswith("  ") and "inputs: v" in h3 and "  source file: raw_hist.nc" in h3)
    yes("without a step, no history", "history" not in WR.provenance(source="x"))
    yes("output path", BC.output_path("d", "vomecrty", "fk", "1993-01") == os.path.join("d", "split", "vomecrty", "vomecrty_fk_1993-01.nc"))
    D = SRC.derived(root, S); yes("derived keeps the grid, tag and step", D.mesh_files == [mesh] and D.tag == "fk" and D.dt == 86400. and D.name == "stage0_raw")
    yes("common and source names find the same files", D.files("u") == D.files("vozocrtx") and len(D.files("u", "2015-01-02")) == 1)
    r = D.read("u", level=None); ok("read back, single precision", np.nan_to_num(r[1] - np.float32(2*u)), 2e-6); yes("read shape", r.shape == (2, nz, ny, nx))
    ok("double precision survives the round trip", np.nan_to_num(D.snapshot(D.files("v")[0], "v", np.float64) + u), 1e-14)
    got = list(D.stream("u", "v", level=1)); yes("stream by common names", [g[0] for g in got] == ["2015-01-01", "2015-01-02"] and got[0][1].shape == (ny, nx))
    os.remove(D.files("v", "2015-01-02")[0]); gr, miss = D.groups("u", "v"); yes("groups keeps common dates and names the others", [g[0] for g in gr] == ["2015-01-01"] and miss == ["2015-01-02"])
    f0 = D.files("u")[0]; ok("time kept", D.time_hours(f0) - 100., 1e-9); ok("depth kept", D.depth(f0) - dep, 1e-5); yes("coordinates kept", D.coords(f0)[0].shape == (ny, nx))
    other = os.path.join(TMP, "stage0_time.nc")
    with netCDF4.Dataset(other, "w") as nc:
        nc.createDimension("time_counter", 1); t = nc.createVariable("time_counter", "f8", ("time_counter",)); t.units, t.calendar = "seconds since 1950-01-02", "gregorian"; t[:] = 3600.
    ok("other time units convert: one day and one hour", D.time_hours(other) - 25., 1e-9)
    for name_ in ("glorys04", "glorys12", "cmems"): yes(f"source finds {name_}", SRC.source(name_).name == name_)

source

Open a raw dataset by name.

Syntax

    gr = S.grid(); M_ = dict(e3u=e3u, e3v=e3v, umask=np.ones_like(u_m), vmask=np.ones_like(v_m), tmask=np.ones_like(u_m), e1t=gr["e1t"], e2t=gr["e2t"], e1v=gr["e1v"], e2u=gr["e2u"])
    M_["e3u"] = M_["e3v"] = e3[:, None, None]*np.ones((nz, ny, nx))
    w_ = WV(np.full((nz, ny, nx), 0.3), np.full((nz, ny, nx), 0.0), M_)
    ok("uniform flow in a periodic channel has no w", w_[:, 1:, 1:-1], 1e-12)
    jj_ = np.arange(ny)[None, :, None]*np.ones((nz, ny, nx)); w_ = WV(np.zeros((nz, ny, nx)), 1e-3*jj_, M_)
    ok("constant divergence gives w by hand, top of the column", w_[0, 3:-3, 3:-3] + 1e-6*e3[:-1].sum(), 1e-12)
    yes("w is NaN on land", np.isnan(WV(np.zeros((nz, ny, nx)), np.zeros((nz, ny, nx)), {**M_, "tmask": tm.astype(bool)})[0, 5, 6]))
    dep_ = WR.write_field(os.path.join(TMP, "stage0_w"), "w", "2015-01-01", w_, lat, lon, 100., "fk", dep, depth_name="depthw")
    with netCDF4.Dataset(dep_) as nc: yes("w files use W levels", nc["vovecrtz"].dimensions == ("depthw", "y", "x"))
    raw_ = os.path.join(TMP, "raw_hist.nc")
    with netCDF4.Dataset(raw_, "w") as nc: nc.history = "made upstream"
    h1 = WR.provenance("PP1 baroclinic: split", raw_)["history"]
    yes("first step: its line, then the raw file and its own history", h1.splitlines()[0].endswith(" | " + os.path.basename(sys.argv[0]) + " " + " ".join(sys.argv[1:])) and "PP1 baroclinic: split" in h1.splitlines()[0] and h1.splitlines()[1:] == ["source file: raw_hist.nc", "made upstream"])
    mid_ = WR.write_field(os.path.join(TMP, "hist"), "u", "2015-01-01", bt, lat, lon, 100., "fk", attrs=WR.provenance("PP1 baroclinic: split", raw_))
    h2 = WR.provenance("PP4 spatial_filter: low", mid_)["history"].splitlines()
    yes("second step goes on top of the first, newest first", "PP4" in h2[0] and "PP1" in h2[1] and h2[2] == "source file: raw_hist.nc")
    yes("no git commit in history", all("git" not in l for l in h2))
    h3 = WR.provenance("PP7 running: cov", {"u": mid_, "v": raw_})["history"].splitlines()
    yes("two inputs keep both histories, indented", h3[1] == "inputs: u" and h3[2].startswith("  ") and "inputs: v" in h3 and "  source file: raw_hist.nc" in h3)
    yes("without a step, no history", "history" not in WR.provenance(source="x"))
    yes("output path", BC.output_path("d", "vomecrty", "fk", "1993-01") == os.path.join("d", "split", "vomecrty", "vomecrty_fk_1993-01.nc"))
    D = SRC.derived(root, S); yes("derived keeps the grid, tag and step", D.mesh_files == [mesh] and D.tag == "fk" and D.dt == 86400. and D.name == "stage0_raw")
    yes("common and source names find the same files", D.files("u") == D.files("vozocrtx") and len(D.files("u", "2015-01-02")) == 1)
    r = D.read("u", level=None); ok("read back, single precision", np.nan_to_num(r[1] - np.float32(2*u)), 2e-6); yes("read shape", r.shape == (2, nz, ny, nx))
    ok("double precision survives the round trip", np.nan_to_num(D.snapshot(D.files("v")[0], "v", np.float64) + u), 1e-14)
    got = list(D.stream("u", "v", level=1)); yes("stream by common names", [g[0] for g in got] == ["2015-01-01", "2015-01-02"] and got[0][1].shape == (ny, nx))
    os.remove(D.files("v", "2015-01-02")[0]); gr, miss = D.groups("u", "v"); yes("groups keeps common dates and names the others", [g[0] for g in gr] == ["2015-01-01"] and miss == ["2015-01-02"])
    f0 = D.files("u")[0]; ok("time kept", D.time_hours(f0) - 100., 1e-9); ok("depth kept", D.depth(f0) - dep, 1e-5); yes("coordinates kept", D.coords(f0)[0].shape == (ny, nx))
    other = os.path.join(TMP, "stage0_time.nc")
    with netCDF4.Dataset(other, "w") as nc:
        nc.createDimension("time_counter", 1); t = nc.createVariable("time_counter", "f8", ("time_counter",)); t.units, t.calendar = "seconds since 1950-01-02", "gregorian"; t[:] = 3600.
    ok("other time units convert: one day and one hour", D.time_hours(other) - 25., 1e-9)
    for name_ in ("glorys04", "glorys12", "cmems"): yes(f"source finds {name_}", SRC.source(name_).name == name_)

See also

derived | Source.__init__

py-kits › datakit › _source › derived

derived

Open data written with write_field, on the grid of a raw dataset.

Description

Fields computed from a dataset are on its grid and at its time step, so they read like it. This opens such a folder as a Source of its own, with the mesh, tag and time step of the original.

$$\text{Source}(\text{name},\ \text{root},\ \text{like.mesh},\ \text{like.tag},\ \text{like.}\Delta t)$$

Syntax

source = derived(root, like)source = derived(root, like, name=None)

Input Arguments

root — str
Folder written by the step, holding <var>/<var>_*.nc
like — str
Raw dataset, or its Source, whose mesh, tag and time step the data share
name — str — default None
Dataset name; the folder's name by default

Output Arguments

source — Source
The derived dataset

Example

Sp = SRC.derived(os.path.join(TMP, "stage0_split"), S)
D = SRC.derived(root, S); yes("derived keeps the grid, tag and step", D.mesh_files == [mesh] and D.tag == "fk" and D.dt == 86400. and D.name == "stage0_raw")

with test(*[f"datakit._source.Source.{m}" for m in ("__init__", "files", "read", "stream", "groups", "mesh", "grid", "vertical", "coords", "depth", "time_hours", "snapshot")], "datakit._source.source", "datakit._source.derived", "datakit._write.write_field", "datakit._write.provenance", "datakit._write.history", "preprocessing.baroclinic.split", "orcakit.grid_c.vertical_velocity", "datakit._source.Source.point_mask", "datakit._source.Source.point_coords", "orcakit.paths.get"):

        for d, s in (("t", 1), ("z", nz), ("y", ny), ("x", nx)): nc.createDimension(d, s)
        nc.createVariable("e3t_0", "f8", ("t", "z"))[:] = e3
        nc.createVariable("e3t_ps", "f8", ("t", "y", "x"))[:] = e3[-1]
        for n_, a in (("tmask", tm), ("umask", um), ("vmask", vm)): nc.createVariable(n_, "i1", ("t", "z", "y", "x"))[:] = a
        for n_ in ("gphit", "glamt", "gphiu", "glamu", "e1t", "e2t", "e1u", "e2u", "e1v", "e2v", "e1f", "e2f"): nc.createVariable(n_, "f8", ("t", "y", "x"))[:] = 1000.
    S = SRC.Source("fake", os.path.join(TMP, "stage0_raw"), [mesh], "fk", 86400.)
    e3u, e3v, u_m, v_m = S.vertical(np.float64)
    yes("masks returned as boolean", u_m.dtype == bool and v_m.dtype == bool)
    ok("e3u is e3t_0 on wet points", (e3u - e3[:, None, None])[:, 1:-2, 1:-2][u_m[:, 1:-2, 1:-2]], 1e-12)
    ok("e3v is e3t_0 on wet points", (e3v - e3[:, None, None])[:, 1:-2, 1:-2][v_m[:, 1:-2, 1:-2]], 1e-12)
    g_ = S.grid(); yes("grid names the boundary and the metrics", g_["boundary"] == "t-fold" and g_["e1u"].shape == (ny, nx) and g_["lat"].shape == (ny, nx))
    yes("mesh reads by name", S.mesh("e3t_0").shape == (nz,))
    try:
        SRC.Source("f", "", [mesh], "f", 1., boundary="closed").vertical(); yes("other boundaries refused", False)
    except NotImplementedError:
        yes("other boundaries refused", True)
    u = 0.1*np.arange(1., nz*ny*nx + 1).reshape(nz, ny, nx)/(nz*ny*nx); u[:, 5, 6] = np.nan
    bt, bc = BC.split(u, e3u, u_m)
    w = e3u*u_m; ok("baroclinic part has zero weighted depth mean", np.nansum(np.nan_to_num(bc)*w, axis=0), 1e-11)
    wet = u_m.all(axis=0); ok("the parts rebuild the field", (bc + bt[None] - u)[:, wet], 1e-12)
    ok("barotropic is the weighted mean, hand value", bt[0, 0] - np.sum(u[:, 0, 0]*e3)/e3.sum(), 1e-12)
    yes("land is NaN in both parts", np.isnan(bc[0, 5, 6]) and np.isnan(bt[5, 6]) and (np.isnan(bc) == ~u_m).all())

    lat, lon = np.zeros((ny, nx)), np.zeros((ny, nx)); dep = np.array([5., 20., 45.]); root = S.root
    for i, date in enumerate(("2015-01-01", "2015-01-02")):
        for var, sign in (("u", 1.), ("v", -1.)):

See also

source | write_field

py-kits › datakit

_write

Write fields in the common file convention: one variable and date per file, NEMO names, time in hours since 1950-01-01, NaN on land, and the history of how each file was made.

Functions

historyThe history a new file inherits from what it read.
history.oneThe history one input passes on.
provenanceThe global attributes saying how a file was made.
write_fieldWrite one snapshot in the common file convention.
py-kits › datakit › _write › history

history

The history a new file inherits from what it read.

Description

A file records every step that made it in its history attribute, newest first, so this collects the history of its inputs. A file written by write_field passes on its own; a raw file passes on its name and, if it has one, its own history.

Several inputs whose histories may differ, such as u and v, are listed one after the other, each under its label and indented.

$$H = \text{history}(\text{input}),\ \text{or}\ \bigoplus_\ell \big[\ \text{inputs: } \ell \ \oplus\ \text{indent}(H_\ell)\ \big]$$

Syntax

history = history(inputs)

Input Arguments

inputs — str
Path read, or {label: path} for several inputs whose histories may differ; each is then listed under 'inputs: <label>', indented

Output Arguments

history — str
Lines, newest first

Example

Whole test
with test(*[f"datakit._source.Source.{m}" for m in ("__init__", "files", "read", "stream", "groups", "mesh", "grid", "vertical", "coords", "depth", "time_hours", "snapshot")], "datakit._source.source", "datakit._source.derived", "datakit._write.write_field", "datakit._write.provenance", "datakit._write.history", "preprocessing.baroclinic.split", "orcakit.grid_c.vertical_velocity", "datakit._source.Source.point_mask", "datakit._source.Source.point_coords", "orcakit.paths.get"):
    from orcakit import paths as PA
    toml = os.path.join(TMP, "paths.toml")
    with open(toml, "w") as t_: t_.write('one = "~/x"\n')
    saved = os.environ.get("LU_PATHS"); os.environ["LU_PATHS"] = toml
    yes("location read, with ~ expanded", PA.get("one") == os.path.expanduser("~/x"))
    yes("unset location gives a placeholder that names it", "two" in PA.get("two") and "not set" in PA.get("two"))
    if saved is None: del os.environ["LU_PATHS"]
    else: os.environ["LU_PATHS"] = saved
    nz, ny, nx = 3, 12, 16; e3 = np.array([10., 20., 30.]); mesh = os.path.join(TMP, "stage0_mesh.nc")
    tm = np.ones((nz, ny, nx), "i1"); tm[:, 5, 6] = 0
    um = tm*np.roll(tm, -1, axis=2); vm = tm*np.roll(tm, -1, axis=1)
    with netCDF4.Dataset(mesh, "w") as nc:
        for d, s in (("t", 1), ("z", nz), ("y", ny), ("x", nx)): nc.createDimension(d, s)
        nc.createVariable("e3t_0", "f8", ("t", "z"))[:] = e3
        nc.createVariable("e3t_ps", "f8", ("t", "y", "x"))[:] = e3[-1]
        for n_, a in (("tmask", tm), ("umask", um), ("vmask", vm)): nc.createVariable(n_, "i1", ("t", "z", "y", "x"))[:] = a
        for n_ in ("gphit", "glamt", "gphiu", "glamu", "e1t", "e2t", "e1u", "e2u", "e1v", "e2v", "e1f", "e2f"): nc.createVariable(n_, "f8", ("t", "y", "x"))[:] = 1000.
    S = SRC.Source("fake", os.path.join(TMP, "stage0_raw"), [mesh], "fk", 86400.)
    e3u, e3v, u_m, v_m = S.vertical(np.float64)
    yes("masks returned as boolean", u_m.dtype == bool and v_m.dtype == bool)
    ok("e3u is e3t_0 on wet points", (e3u - e3[:, None, None])[:, 1:-2, 1:-2][u_m[:, 1:-2, 1:-2]], 1e-12)
    ok("e3v is e3t_0 on wet points", (e3v - e3[:, None, None])[:, 1:-2, 1:-2][v_m[:, 1:-2, 1:-2]], 1e-12)
    g_ = S.grid(); yes("grid names the boundary and the metrics", g_["boundary"] == "t-fold" and g_["e1u"].shape == (ny, nx) and g_["lat"].shape == (ny, nx))
    yes("mesh reads by name", S.mesh("e3t_0").shape == (nz,))
    try:
        SRC.Source("f", "", [mesh], "f", 1., boundary="closed").vertical(); yes("other boundaries refused", False)
    except NotImplementedError:
        yes("other boundaries refused", True)
    u = 0.1*np.arange(1., nz*ny*nx + 1).reshape(nz, ny, nx)/(nz*ny*nx); u[:, 5, 6] = np.nan
    bt, bc = BC.split(u, e3u, u_m)
    w = e3u*u_m; ok("baroclinic part has zero weighted depth mean", np.nansum(np.nan_to_num(bc)*w, axis=0), 1e-11)
    wet = u_m.all(axis=0); ok("the parts rebuild the field", (bc + bt[None] - u)[:, wet], 1e-12)
    ok("barotropic is the weighted mean, hand value", bt[0, 0] - np.sum(u[:, 0, 0]*e3)/e3.sum(), 1e-12)
    yes("land is NaN in both parts", np.isnan(bc[0, 5, 6]) and np.isnan(bt[5, 6]) and (np.isnan(bc) == ~u_m).all())
    attrs = WR.provenance(source="fake"); yes("provenance has commit, command, date and extras", all(k in attrs for k in ("git_commit", "command", "created", "source")))
    lat, lon = np.zeros((ny, nx)), np.zeros((ny, nx)); dep = np.array([5., 20., 45.]); root = S.root
    for i, date in enumerate(("2015-01-01", "2015-01-02")):
        for var, sign in (("u", 1.), ("v", -1.)):
            p = WR.write_field(root, var, date, sign*(i + 1)*u, lat, lon, 100. + i, "fk", dep, np.float64 if var == "v" else np.float32, attrs)
    yes("path follows the convention", p.endswith(os.path.join("vomecrty", "vomecrty_fk_2015-01-02.nc")) and not glob.glob(p + ".tmp*"))
    with netCDF4.Dataset(p) as nc:
        yes("file convention", nc["vomecrty"].dimensions == ("deptht", "y", "x") and nc["time_counter"].shape == () and np.isnan(nc["vomecrty"]._FillValue) and nc["vomecrty"].filters()["zlib"] and nc["vomecrty"].dtype == np.float64 and nc.source == "fake")
    bt_path = WR.write_field(os.path.join(TMP, "stage0_bt"), "v", "2015-01-01", bt, lat, lon, 100., "fk")
    with netCDF4.Dataset(bt_path) as nc: yes("2D field has no depth", nc["vomecrty"].dimensions == ("y", "x"))
    both = WR.write_field(os.path.join(TMP, "stage0_split"), "v", "2015-01-01", bc, lat, lon, 100., "fk", dep, np.float64, attrs, {"vobtcrty": bt})
    Sp = SRC.derived(os.path.join(TMP, "stage0_split"), S)
    yes("both parts share one file", Sp.files("vbt") == Sp.files("v") == [both])
    with netCDF4.Dataset(both) as nc: yes("barotropic part is 2D, baroclinic 3D, same type", nc["vobtcrty"].dimensions == ("y", "x") and nc["vomecrty"].dimensions == ("deptht", "y", "x") and nc["vobtcrty"].dtype == np.float64)
    ok("barotropic part reads back by common name", np.nan_to_num(Sp.read("vbt")[0] - np.float32(bt)), 1e-6)
    ok("baroclinic part reads back by common name", np.nan_to_num(Sp.read("v", level=None)[0] - np.float32(bc)), 1e-6)
    import _common as CM
    yes("resume accepts the same precision", not CM.incompatible(both, ("vomecrty", "vobtcrty"), np.float64))
    yes("resume refuses another precision", CM.incompatible(both, ("vomecrty", "vobtcrty"), np.float32))
    yes("resume refuses a file with one part", CM.incompatible(p, ("vomecrty", "vobtcrty"), np.float64))
    WV = lambda a, b, m: grid_c.vertical_velocity(a, b, exchange=orca.halo, **m)
    yes("point mask by name", S.point_mask("U").dtype == bool)
    pc = S.point_coords("U"); yes("point coordinates from the mesh", len(pc) == 2 and pc[0].shape == (ny, nx))
    gr = S.grid(); M_ = dict(e3u=e3u, e3v=e3v, umask=np.ones_like(u_m), vmask=np.ones_like(v_m), tmask=np.ones_like(u_m), e1t=gr["e1t"], e2t=gr["e2t"], e1v=gr["e1v"], e2u=gr["e2u"])
    M_["e3u"] = M_["e3v"] = e3[:, None, None]*np.ones((nz, ny, nx))
    w_ = WV(np.full((nz, ny, nx), 0.3), np.full((nz, ny, nx), 0.0), M_)
    ok("uniform flow in a periodic channel has no w", w_[:, 1:, 1:-1], 1e-12)
    jj_ = np.arange(ny)[None, :, None]*np.ones((nz, ny, nx)); w_ = WV(np.zeros((nz, ny, nx)), 1e-3*jj_, M_)
    ok("constant divergence gives w by hand, top of the column", w_[0, 3:-3, 3:-3] + 1e-6*e3[:-1].sum(), 1e-12)
    yes("w is NaN on land", np.isnan(WV(np.zeros((nz, ny, nx)), np.zeros((nz, ny, nx)), {**M_, "tmask": tm.astype(bool)})[0, 5, 6]))
    dep_ = WR.write_field(os.path.join(TMP, "stage0_w"), "w", "2015-01-01", w_, lat, lon, 100., "fk", dep, depth_name="depthw")
    with netCDF4.Dataset(dep_) as nc: yes("w files use W levels", nc["vovecrtz"].dimensions == ("depthw", "y", "x"))
    raw_ = os.path.join(TMP, "raw_hist.nc")
    with netCDF4.Dataset(raw_, "w") as nc: nc.history = "made upstream"
    h1 = WR.provenance("PP1 baroclinic: split", raw_)["history"]
    yes("first step: its line, then the raw file and its own history", h1.splitlines()[0].endswith(" | " + os.path.basename(sys.argv[0]) + " " + " ".join(sys.argv[1:])) and "PP1 baroclinic: split" in h1.splitlines()[0] and h1.splitlines()[1:] == ["source file: raw_hist.nc", "made upstream"])
    mid_ = WR.write_field(os.path.join(TMP, "hist"), "u", "2015-01-01", bt, lat, lon, 100., "fk", attrs=WR.provenance("PP1 baroclinic: split", raw_))
    h2 = WR.provenance("PP4 spatial_filter: low", mid_)["history"].splitlines()
    yes("second step goes on top of the first, newest first", "PP4" in h2[0] and "PP1" in h2[1] and h2[2] == "source file: raw_hist.nc")
    yes("no git commit in history", all("git" not in l for l in h2))
    h3 = WR.provenance("PP7 running: cov", {"u": mid_, "v": raw_})["history"].splitlines()
    yes("two inputs keep both histories, indented", h3[1] == "inputs: u" and h3[2].startswith("  ") and "inputs: v" in h3 and "  source file: raw_hist.nc" in h3)
    yes("without a step, no history", "history" not in WR.provenance(source="x"))
    yes("output path", BC.output_path("d", "vomecrty", "fk", "1993-01") == os.path.join("d", "split", "vomecrty", "vomecrty_fk_1993-01.nc"))
    D = SRC.derived(root, S); yes("derived keeps the grid, tag and step", D.mesh_files == [mesh] and D.tag == "fk" and D.dt == 86400. and D.name == "stage0_raw")
    yes("common and source names find the same files", D.files("u") == D.files("vozocrtx") and len(D.files("u", "2015-01-02")) == 1)
    r = D.read("u", level=None); ok("read back, single precision", np.nan_to_num(r[1] - np.float32(2*u)), 2e-6); yes("read shape", r.shape == (2, nz, ny, nx))
    ok("double precision survives the round trip", np.nan_to_num(D.snapshot(D.files("v")[0], "v", np.float64) + u), 1e-14)
    got = list(D.stream("u", "v", level=1)); yes("stream by common names", [g[0] for g in got] == ["2015-01-01", "2015-01-02"] and got[0][1].shape == (ny, nx))
    os.remove(D.files("v", "2015-01-02")[0]); gr, miss = D.groups("u", "v"); yes("groups keeps common dates and names the others", [g[0] for g in gr] == ["2015-01-01"] and miss == ["2015-01-02"])
    f0 = D.files("u")[0]; ok("time kept", D.time_hours(f0) - 100., 1e-9); ok("depth kept", D.depth(f0) - dep, 1e-5); yes("coordinates kept", D.coords(f0)[0].shape == (ny, nx))
    other = os.path.join(TMP, "stage0_time.nc")
    with netCDF4.Dataset(other, "w") as nc:
        nc.createDimension("time_counter", 1); t = nc.createVariable("time_counter", "f8", ("time_counter",)); t.units, t.calendar = "seconds since 1950-01-02", "gregorian"; t[:] = 3600.
    ok("other time units convert: one day and one hour", D.time_hours(other) - 25., 1e-9)
    for name_ in ("glorys04", "glorys12", "cmems"): yes(f"source finds {name_}", SRC.source(name_).name == name_)

provenance in py-kits/datakit/_write.py: The global attributes saying how a file was made.

out["history"] += "\n" + history(inputs)

See also

provenance

py-kits › datakit › _write › history.one

history.one

The history one input passes on.

Description

$$H = \text{history attribute, or ``source file: name'' and its own history}$$

Syntax

history = one(path)

Input Arguments

path — str
File read

Output Arguments

history — str
Its history attribute if a pipeline step wrote it; otherwise its name, then its own history if any

Example

No test of its own; see the routines that call it.

See also

history

py-kits › datakit › _write › provenance

provenance

The global attributes saying how a file was made.

Description

A result is only useful if it can be traced back: the commit and command that made it, when, from what. With a step, the history attribute gets one line, the date, the step and the command, above the history of the inputs, so a file carries its whole chain of steps down to the raw data.

$$\text{history} = \text{date}\ \text{step}\ |\ \text{command} \ \oplus\ \text{history}(\text{inputs})$$

Syntax

attrs = provenance()attrs = provenance(step=None, inputs=None)

Input Arguments

step — str — default None
e.g. 'PP5 coarse_grain: bin onto domain_cfg.nc', or None
inputs — str — default None
File read, or {label: path}; used with step **extra : Further attributes, e.g. source='cmems'

Output Arguments

attrs — dict
git_commit, command, created; with a step also processing, history and source_file; then extra

Example

h1 = WR.provenance("PP1 baroclinic: split", raw_)["history"]
mid_ = WR.write_field(os.path.join(TMP, "hist"), "u", "2015-01-01", bt, lat, lon, 100., "fk", attrs=WR.provenance("PP1 baroclinic: split", raw_))
h2 = WR.provenance("PP4 spatial_filter: low", mid_)["history"].splitlines()
h3 = WR.provenance("PP7 running: cov", {"u": mid_, "v": raw_})["history"].splitlines()
yes("without a step, no history", "history" not in WR.provenance(source="x"))

    jj_ = np.arange(ny)[None, :, None]*np.ones((nz, ny, nx)); w_ = WV(np.zeros((nz, ny, nx)), 1e-3*jj_, M_)
    ok("constant divergence gives w by hand, top of the column", w_[0, 3:-3, 3:-3] + 1e-6*e3[:-1].sum(), 1e-12)
    yes("w is NaN on land", np.isnan(WV(np.zeros((nz, ny, nx)), np.zeros((nz, ny, nx)), {**M_, "tmask": tm.astype(bool)})[0, 5, 6]))
    dep_ = WR.write_field(os.path.join(TMP, "stage0_w"), "w", "2015-01-01", w_, lat, lon, 100., "fk", dep, depth_name="depthw")
    with netCDF4.Dataset(dep_) as nc: yes("w files use W levels", nc["vovecrtz"].dimensions == ("depthw", "y", "x"))
    raw_ = os.path.join(TMP, "raw_hist.nc")
    with netCDF4.Dataset(raw_, "w") as nc: nc.history = "made upstream"
    h1 = WR.provenance("PP1 baroclinic: split", raw_)["history"]
    yes("first step: its line, then the raw file and its own history", h1.splitlines()[0].endswith(" | " + os.path.basename(sys.argv[0]) + " " + " ".join(sys.argv[1:])) and "PP1 baroclinic: split" in h1.splitlines()[0] and h1.splitlines()[1:] == ["source file: raw_hist.nc", "made upstream"])
    mid_ = WR.write_field(os.path.join(TMP, "hist"), "u", "2015-01-01", bt, lat, lon, 100., "fk", attrs=WR.provenance("PP1 baroclinic: split", raw_))
    h2 = WR.provenance("PP4 spatial_filter: low", mid_)["history"].splitlines()
    yes("second step goes on top of the first, newest first", "PP4" in h2[0] and "PP1" in h2[1] and h2[2] == "source file: raw_hist.nc")
    yes("no git commit in history", all("git" not in l for l in h2))
    h3 = WR.provenance("PP7 running: cov", {"u": mid_, "v": raw_})["history"].splitlines()
    yes("two inputs keep both histories, indented", h3[1] == "inputs: u" and h3[2].startswith("  ") and "inputs: v" in h3 and "  source file: raw_hist.nc" in h3)
    yes("without a step, no history", "history" not in WR.provenance(source="x"))
    yes("output path", BC.output_path("d", "vomecrty", "fk", "1993-01") == os.path.join("d", "split", "vomecrty", "vomecrty_fk_1993-01.nc"))
    D = SRC.derived(root, S); yes("derived keeps the grid, tag and step", D.mesh_files == [mesh] and D.tag == "fk" and D.dt == 86400. and D.name == "stage0_raw")
    yes("common and source names find the same files", D.files("u") == D.files("vozocrtx") and len(D.files("u", "2015-01-02")) == 1)
    r = D.read("u", level=None); ok("read back, single precision", np.nan_to_num(r[1] - np.float32(2*u)), 2e-6); yes("read shape", r.shape == (2, nz, ny, nx))
    ok("double precision survives the round trip", np.nan_to_num(D.snapshot(D.files("v")[0], "v", np.float64) + u), 1e-14)
    got = list(D.stream("u", "v", level=1)); yes("stream by common names", [g[0] for g in got] == ["2015-01-01", "2015-01-02"] and got[0][1].shape == (ny, nx))
    os.remove(D.files("v", "2015-01-02")[0]); gr, miss = D.groups("u", "v"); yes("groups keeps common dates and names the others", [g[0] for g in gr] == ["2015-01-01"] and miss == ["2015-01-02"])
    f0 = D.files("u")[0]; ok("time kept", D.time_hours(f0) - 100., 1e-9); ok("depth kept", D.depth(f0) - dep, 1e-5); yes("coordinates kept", D.coords(f0)[0].shape == (ny, nx))
    other = os.path.join(TMP, "stage0_time.nc")
    with netCDF4.Dataset(other, "w") as nc:
        nc.createDimension("time_counter", 1); t = nc.createVariable("time_counter", "f8", ("time_counter",)); t.units, t.calendar = "seconds since 1950-01-02", "gregorian"; t[:] = 3600.
    ok("other time units convert: one day and one hour", D.time_hours(other) - 25., 1e-9)
    for name_ in ("glorys04", "glorys12", "cmems"): yes(f"source finds {name_}", SRC.source(name_).name == name_)

history | write_field

py-kits › datakit › _write › write_field

write_field

Write one snapshot in the common file convention.

Description

Every result written this way reads back like a raw dataset: root/<var>/<var>_<tag>_<date>.nc, NEMO's variable names, a scalar time in hours since 1950-01-01, NaN as fill value, compressed and chunked. Extra variables, such as a barotropic part, can share the file.

The file is written under a temporary name and then renamed, so a stopped run never leaves a partial file behind.

$$\text{root}/v/v\_\text{tag}\_\text{date}.nc \leftarrow \{v:\ x,\ \text{extra},\ \varphi,\ \lambda,\ t,\ z\}$$

Syntax

path = write_field(root, var, date, field, lat, lon, time_hours, tag)path = write_field(root, var, date, field, lat, lon, time_hours, tag, depth=None, dtype=np.float32, attrs=None, extra=None, depth_name='deptht')

Input Arguments

root — str
Folder of the dataset written
var — str
Common or NEMO name of the variable
date — str
Date in the file name
field — float
(ny, nx), or (nz, ny, nx) with depth; land as NaN
lat — float
(ny, nx) latitude of the field's points
lon — float
(ny, nx) longitude of the field's points
time_hours — float
Time, in hours since 1950-01-01
tag — str
Tag in the file name
depth — float — default None
(nz,) levels, for a 3D field
dtype — dtype — default np.float32
Stored type
attrs — dict — default None
Global attributes, see provenance
extra — dict — default None
{name: field} also stored in this file, e.g. the barotropic part
depth_name — str — default 'deptht'
'deptht', or 'depthw' for fields at the top of the T-cells

Output Arguments

path — str
The file written

Example

p = WR.write_field(root, var, date, sign*(i + 1)*u, lat, lon, 100. + i, "fk", dep, np.float64 if var == "v" else np.float32, attrs)
bt_path = WR.write_field(os.path.join(TMP, "stage0_bt"), "v", "2015-01-01", bt, lat, lon, 100., "fk")
both = WR.write_field(os.path.join(TMP, "stage0_split"), "v", "2015-01-01", bc, lat, lon, 100., "fk", dep, np.float64, attrs, {"vobtcrty": bt})
dep_ = WR.write_field(os.path.join(TMP, "stage0_w"), "w", "2015-01-01", w_, lat, lon, 100., "fk", dep, depth_name="depthw")
mid_ = WR.write_field(os.path.join(TMP, "hist"), "u", "2015-01-01", bt, lat, lon, 100., "fk", attrs=WR.provenance("PP1 baroclinic: split", raw_))
Whole test
with test(*[f"datakit._source.Source.{m}" for m in ("__init__", "files", "read", "stream", "groups", "mesh", "grid", "vertical", "coords", "depth", "time_hours", "snapshot")], "datakit._source.source", "datakit._source.derived", "datakit._write.write_field", "datakit._write.provenance", "datakit._write.history", "preprocessing.baroclinic.split", "orcakit.grid_c.vertical_velocity", "datakit._source.Source.point_mask", "datakit._source.Source.point_coords", "orcakit.paths.get"):
    from orcakit import paths as PA
    toml = os.path.join(TMP, "paths.toml")
    with open(toml, "w") as t_: t_.write('one = "~/x"\n')
    saved = os.environ.get("LU_PATHS"); os.environ["LU_PATHS"] = toml
    yes("location read, with ~ expanded", PA.get("one") == os.path.expanduser("~/x"))
    yes("unset location gives a placeholder that names it", "two" in PA.get("two") and "not set" in PA.get("two"))
    if saved is None: del os.environ["LU_PATHS"]
    else: os.environ["LU_PATHS"] = saved
    nz, ny, nx = 3, 12, 16; e3 = np.array([10., 20., 30.]); mesh = os.path.join(TMP, "stage0_mesh.nc")
    tm = np.ones((nz, ny, nx), "i1"); tm[:, 5, 6] = 0
    um = tm*np.roll(tm, -1, axis=2); vm = tm*np.roll(tm, -1, axis=1)
    with netCDF4.Dataset(mesh, "w") as nc:
        for d, s in (("t", 1), ("z", nz), ("y", ny), ("x", nx)): nc.createDimension(d, s)
        nc.createVariable("e3t_0", "f8", ("t", "z"))[:] = e3
        nc.createVariable("e3t_ps", "f8", ("t", "y", "x"))[:] = e3[-1]
        for n_, a in (("tmask", tm), ("umask", um), ("vmask", vm)): nc.createVariable(n_, "i1", ("t", "z", "y", "x"))[:] = a
        for n_ in ("gphit", "glamt", "gphiu", "glamu", "e1t", "e2t", "e1u", "e2u", "e1v", "e2v", "e1f", "e2f"): nc.createVariable(n_, "f8", ("t", "y", "x"))[:] = 1000.
    S = SRC.Source("fake", os.path.join(TMP, "stage0_raw"), [mesh], "fk", 86400.)
    e3u, e3v, u_m, v_m = S.vertical(np.float64)
    yes("masks returned as boolean", u_m.dtype == bool and v_m.dtype == bool)
    ok("e3u is e3t_0 on wet points", (e3u - e3[:, None, None])[:, 1:-2, 1:-2][u_m[:, 1:-2, 1:-2]], 1e-12)
    ok("e3v is e3t_0 on wet points", (e3v - e3[:, None, None])[:, 1:-2, 1:-2][v_m[:, 1:-2, 1:-2]], 1e-12)
    g_ = S.grid(); yes("grid names the boundary and the metrics", g_["boundary"] == "t-fold" and g_["e1u"].shape == (ny, nx) and g_["lat"].shape == (ny, nx))
    yes("mesh reads by name", S.mesh("e3t_0").shape == (nz,))
    try:
        SRC.Source("f", "", [mesh], "f", 1., boundary="closed").vertical(); yes("other boundaries refused", False)
    except NotImplementedError:
        yes("other boundaries refused", True)
    u = 0.1*np.arange(1., nz*ny*nx + 1).reshape(nz, ny, nx)/(nz*ny*nx); u[:, 5, 6] = np.nan
    bt, bc = BC.split(u, e3u, u_m)
    w = e3u*u_m; ok("baroclinic part has zero weighted depth mean", np.nansum(np.nan_to_num(bc)*w, axis=0), 1e-11)
    wet = u_m.all(axis=0); ok("the parts rebuild the field", (bc + bt[None] - u)[:, wet], 1e-12)
    ok("barotropic is the weighted mean, hand value", bt[0, 0] - np.sum(u[:, 0, 0]*e3)/e3.sum(), 1e-12)
    yes("land is NaN in both parts", np.isnan(bc[0, 5, 6]) and np.isnan(bt[5, 6]) and (np.isnan(bc) == ~u_m).all())
    attrs = WR.provenance(source="fake"); yes("provenance has commit, command, date and extras", all(k in attrs for k in ("git_commit", "command", "created", "source")))
    lat, lon = np.zeros((ny, nx)), np.zeros((ny, nx)); dep = np.array([5., 20., 45.]); root = S.root
    for i, date in enumerate(("2015-01-01", "2015-01-02")):
        for var, sign in (("u", 1.), ("v", -1.)):
            p = WR.write_field(root, var, date, sign*(i + 1)*u, lat, lon, 100. + i, "fk", dep, np.float64 if var == "v" else np.float32, attrs)
    yes("path follows the convention", p.endswith(os.path.join("vomecrty", "vomecrty_fk_2015-01-02.nc")) and not glob.glob(p + ".tmp*"))
    with netCDF4.Dataset(p) as nc:
        yes("file convention", nc["vomecrty"].dimensions == ("deptht", "y", "x") and nc["time_counter"].shape == () and np.isnan(nc["vomecrty"]._FillValue) and nc["vomecrty"].filters()["zlib"] and nc["vomecrty"].dtype == np.float64 and nc.source == "fake")
    bt_path = WR.write_field(os.path.join(TMP, "stage0_bt"), "v", "2015-01-01", bt, lat, lon, 100., "fk")
    with netCDF4.Dataset(bt_path) as nc: yes("2D field has no depth", nc["vomecrty"].dimensions == ("y", "x"))
    both = WR.write_field(os.path.join(TMP, "stage0_split"), "v", "2015-01-01", bc, lat, lon, 100., "fk", dep, np.float64, attrs, {"vobtcrty": bt})
    Sp = SRC.derived(os.path.join(TMP, "stage0_split"), S)
    yes("both parts share one file", Sp.files("vbt") == Sp.files("v") == [both])
    with netCDF4.Dataset(both) as nc: yes("barotropic part is 2D, baroclinic 3D, same type", nc["vobtcrty"].dimensions == ("y", "x") and nc["vomecrty"].dimensions == ("deptht", "y", "x") and nc["vobtcrty"].dtype == np.float64)
    ok("barotropic part reads back by common name", np.nan_to_num(Sp.read("vbt")[0] - np.float32(bt)), 1e-6)
    ok("baroclinic part reads back by common name", np.nan_to_num(Sp.read("v", level=None)[0] - np.float32(bc)), 1e-6)
    import _common as CM
    yes("resume accepts the same precision", not CM.incompatible(both, ("vomecrty", "vobtcrty"), np.float64))
    yes("resume refuses another precision", CM.incompatible(both, ("vomecrty", "vobtcrty"), np.float32))
    yes("resume refuses a file with one part", CM.incompatible(p, ("vomecrty", "vobtcrty"), np.float64))
    WV = lambda a, b, m: grid_c.vertical_velocity(a, b, exchange=orca.halo, **m)
    yes("point mask by name", S.point_mask("U").dtype == bool)
    pc = S.point_coords("U"); yes("point coordinates from the mesh", len(pc) == 2 and pc[0].shape == (ny, nx))
    gr = S.grid(); M_ = dict(e3u=e3u, e3v=e3v, umask=np.ones_like(u_m), vmask=np.ones_like(v_m), tmask=np.ones_like(u_m), e1t=gr["e1t"], e2t=gr["e2t"], e1v=gr["e1v"], e2u=gr["e2u"])
    M_["e3u"] = M_["e3v"] = e3[:, None, None]*np.ones((nz, ny, nx))
    w_ = WV(np.full((nz, ny, nx), 0.3), np.full((nz, ny, nx), 0.0), M_)
    ok("uniform flow in a periodic channel has no w", w_[:, 1:, 1:-1], 1e-12)
    jj_ = np.arange(ny)[None, :, None]*np.ones((nz, ny, nx)); w_ = WV(np.zeros((nz, ny, nx)), 1e-3*jj_, M_)
    ok("constant divergence gives w by hand, top of the column", w_[0, 3:-3, 3:-3] + 1e-6*e3[:-1].sum(), 1e-12)
    yes("w is NaN on land", np.isnan(WV(np.zeros((nz, ny, nx)), np.zeros((nz, ny, nx)), {**M_, "tmask": tm.astype(bool)})[0, 5, 6]))
    dep_ = WR.write_field(os.path.join(TMP, "stage0_w"), "w", "2015-01-01", w_, lat, lon, 100., "fk", dep, depth_name="depthw")
    with netCDF4.Dataset(dep_) as nc: yes("w files use W levels", nc["vovecrtz"].dimensions == ("depthw", "y", "x"))
    raw_ = os.path.join(TMP, "raw_hist.nc")
    with netCDF4.Dataset(raw_, "w") as nc: nc.history = "made upstream"
    h1 = WR.provenance("PP1 baroclinic: split", raw_)["history"]
    yes("first step: its line, then the raw file and its own history", h1.splitlines()[0].endswith(" | " + os.path.basename(sys.argv[0]) + " " + " ".join(sys.argv[1:])) and "PP1 baroclinic: split" in h1.splitlines()[0] and h1.splitlines()[1:] == ["source file: raw_hist.nc", "made upstream"])
    mid_ = WR.write_field(os.path.join(TMP, "hist"), "u", "2015-01-01", bt, lat, lon, 100., "fk", attrs=WR.provenance("PP1 baroclinic: split", raw_))
    h2 = WR.provenance("PP4 spatial_filter: low", mid_)["history"].splitlines()
    yes("second step goes on top of the first, newest first", "PP4" in h2[0] and "PP1" in h2[1] and h2[2] == "source file: raw_hist.nc")
    yes("no git commit in history", all("git" not in l for l in h2))
    h3 = WR.provenance("PP7 running: cov", {"u": mid_, "v": raw_})["history"].splitlines()
    yes("two inputs keep both histories, indented", h3[1] == "inputs: u" and h3[2].startswith("  ") and "inputs: v" in h3 and "  source file: raw_hist.nc" in h3)
    yes("without a step, no history", "history" not in WR.provenance(source="x"))
    yes("output path", BC.output_path("d", "vomecrty", "fk", "1993-01") == os.path.join("d", "split", "vomecrty", "vomecrty_fk_1993-01.nc"))
    D = SRC.derived(root, S); yes("derived keeps the grid, tag and step", D.mesh_files == [mesh] and D.tag == "fk" and D.dt == 86400. and D.name == "stage0_raw")
    yes("common and source names find the same files", D.files("u") == D.files("vozocrtx") and len(D.files("u", "2015-01-02")) == 1)
    r = D.read("u", level=None); ok("read back, single precision", np.nan_to_num(r[1] - np.float32(2*u)), 2e-6); yes("read shape", r.shape == (2, nz, ny, nx))
    ok("double precision survives the round trip", np.nan_to_num(D.snapshot(D.files("v")[0], "v", np.float64) + u), 1e-14)
    got = list(D.stream("u", "v", level=1)); yes("stream by common names", [g[0] for g in got] == ["2015-01-01", "2015-01-02"] and got[0][1].shape == (ny, nx))
    os.remove(D.files("v", "2015-01-02")[0]); gr, miss = D.groups("u", "v"); yes("groups keeps common dates and names the others", [g[0] for g in gr] == ["2015-01-01"] and miss == ["2015-01-02"])
    f0 = D.files("u")[0]; ok("time kept", D.time_hours(f0) - 100., 1e-9); ok("depth kept", D.depth(f0) - dep, 1e-5); yes("coordinates kept", D.coords(f0)[0].shape == (ny, nx))
    other = os.path.join(TMP, "stage0_time.nc")
    with netCDF4.Dataset(other, "w") as nc:
        nc.createDimension("time_counter", 1); t = nc.createVariable("time_counter", "f8", ("time_counter",)); t.units, t.calendar = "seconds since 1950-01-02", "gregorian"; t[:] = 3600.
    ok("other time units convert: one day and one hour", D.time_hours(other) - 25., 1e-9)

py-kits › datakit

cmems

ORAS5 from CMEMS (1/4 degree, 1021 x 1442, 75 levels), monthly. 2D fields cover 2000-2024; u and v cover 2015-2024.

Variables: sossheig, sosstsst, vozocrtx, vomecrty Dates are 'YYYY-MM-DD' or 'YYYY-MM', inclusive.

Functions

filesThe files of one CMEMS variable between two dates.
readRead a CMEMS variable between two dates into one array.
streamRead several CMEMS variables one snapshot at a time.
meshCMEMS grid fields by name.

py-kits

orcakit

Operations on NEMO's ORCA grids: the C-grid stencils, the seam and fold, masks, filters and parallel tiles.

The ORCA family of global grids is curvilinear and staggered (Arakawa C: tracers at cell centres, velocities on the faces), periodic east-west with two repeated columns, and folded onto itself at the north. Any operation that looks at neighbours, a gradient or a filter, must respect all of that, or it gives wrong values along the seam and near the pole. orcakit gathers those operations once, written to match NEMO's own discretisation, so the rest of the library never handles a boundary by hand.

Every routine takes and returns plain arrays, so it can be used at any step of any computation.

Conventions: north stays at the high y index, as NEMO stores it; flipping the grid, as some older code did, puts the fold on the wrong edge. The seam and fold rules (orca.halo, orca.FOLD) are those of the fine grids with a T-point pivot and two overlap columns, GLORYS04, GLORYS12 and CMEMS; eORCA1's domain file has an F-point pivot and no overlap columns, and must not go through them.

Modules

orcathe seam and the north fold (halo), Gaussian smoothing across them, masks, partial-step thicknesses, the barotropic split, nearest-point search and averaging onto a coarser grid
grid_cC-grid operators: averages between points, differences, divergence, vorticity, vertical velocity by continuity and geostrophic velocity
filtersland-aware low-pass and high-pass in space, on the whole grid or on a tile, and the deseasonalising and Butterworth filters in time
mpi_orcathe domain decomposition into tiles, halo exchange between ranks, and gathering
mpi_filtera stand-alone parallel filter script built on the same ideas, with a check against a whole-domain reference
netcdfwriting fields and modes to NetCDF files with the dimensions of a grid file
pathsdata locations, read from paths.toml
py-kits › orcakit

filters

Filters as primitives: arrays in, arrays out, for any field at any step. Space: lowpass, highpass, lowpass_tile, and masked_smooth and scale_split, which keep land as 0. Time: deseason, time_lowpass.

Scale separation via spatial low-pass filtering: a mask-aware smoothing that isolates the large-scale field, and (field - large_scale) as the small-scale residual. Grid-generic -- the actual smoothing kernel (e.g. ORCA's Gaussian smooth_2D with north-fold handling) is injected as a callable, same pattern as grid_c.py's `exchange`.

smooth signature: smooth(field, sigma) -> smoothed_field

Functions

masked_smoothLow-pass a field without letting masked points, such as land, bias it near the mask edge.
scale_splitSplit a field into a large-scale part and the small-scale residual.
gaussianGaussian smoothing in the last two axes of a field that already carries its halo.
lowpassGaussian low-pass in space over valid points only, for fields or statistics.
highpassGaussian high-pass in space, the field minus its low-pass.
lowpass_tileLowpass on one rank's tile of a domain decomposition.
deseasonRemove, point by point, the mean, a linear trend and the harmonics of a period.
time_lowpassZero-phase Butterworth low-pass in time, along axis 0.
py-kits › orcakit › filters › masked_smooth

masked_smooth

Low-pass a field without letting masked points, such as land, bias it near the mask edge.

Description

Smoothing a field with zeros on land pulls the result towards zero along every coast, since the kernel averages those zeros in. Here the field times the mask and the mask itself are smoothed with the same kernel and divided, which is a local average over valid points only.

Where under 1% of the kernel's footprint is valid the ratio divides a tiny number by a tiny number: near the ORCA north fold this once turned v = -0.006 m/s into -325 m/s. Those points are set to 0, as are masked points. lowpass does the same with NaN in place of 0.

$$\tilde f = \frac{G_\sigma * (f\,m)}{G_\sigma * m}\;m \quad\text{where } G_\sigma * m > 0.01,\ \text{else } 0$$

Syntax

field_out = masked_smooth(field_in, mask, sigma, smooth)field_out = masked_smooth(field_in, mask, sigma, smooth, smooth_mask=None)

Input Arguments

field_in — float
Field to be smoothed
mask — float
1 for valid (e.g. ocean) points, 0 elsewhere; broadcastable against field_in's trailing two axes
sigma — float
Filter lengthscale, in gridpoints
smooth — callable
smooth(field, sigma) -> smoothed_field, e.g. functools.partial(orca.smooth_2D, mask=None) -- this routine handles masking itself, so the injected smooth should not also mask internally
smooth_mask — callable — default None
smooth for the mask, default `smooth`. Needed when `smooth` flips the sign at the north fold: a mask must never flip

Output Arguments

field_out — float
Smoothed field, zeroed both on masked points and wherever the filter footprint found no valid neighbour at all

Example

ok("constant stays exact next to land", (filters.masked_smooth(7*mk, mk, 4., sm) - 7)[mk > 0], 1e-11)
ok("land stays 0", filters.masked_smooth(7*mk, mk, 4., sm)[mk == 0], 0)
ok("wave far from land", rerr(filters.masked_smooth(f, np.ones_like(f), 4., sm)[20:-20], (np.exp(-8*k*k)*f)[20:-20]), 2e-3)
ok("a mask of ones gives den = 1 at the fold", filters.masked_smooth(one, one, 4., keep, keep) - 1, 1e-11)
ok("with smooth_mask, a flipped field leaves den alone", np.abs(filters.masked_smooth(one, one, 4., flip, keep)[-1]).max() - (orca.smooth_2D(one, 4., isMeridional=True)[-1]).max(), 1e-11)
Whole test
with test("orcakit.filters.masked_smooth", "orcakit.filters.scale_split"):
    ny, nx = 90, 240; mk = np.ones((ny, nx)); mk[30:50, 60:100] = 0; sm = partial(orca.smooth_2D, mask=None)
    ok("constant stays exact next to land", (filters.masked_smooth(7*mk, mk, 4., sm) - 7)[mk > 0], 1e-11)
    ok("land stays 0", filters.masked_smooth(7*mk, mk, 4., sm)[mk == 0], 0)
    k = 2*np.pi*6/(nx-2); f = np.cos(k*np.arange(nx))[None]*np.ones((ny, nx))
    ok("wave far from land", rerr(filters.masked_smooth(f, np.ones_like(f), 4., sm)[20:-20], (np.exp(-8*k*k)*f)[20:-20]), 2e-3)
    ny7, nx7 = 60, 120; one = np.ones((ny7, nx7)); flip = partial(orca.smooth_2D, mask=None, isMeridional=True); keep = partial(orca.smooth_2D, mask=None)
    ok("a mask of ones gives den = 1 at the fold", filters.masked_smooth(one, one, 4., keep, keep) - 1, 1e-11)
    ok("with smooth_mask, a flipped field leaves den alone", np.abs(filters.masked_smooth(one, one, 4., flip, keep)[-1]).max() - (orca.smooth_2D(one, 4., isMeridional=True)[-1]).max(), 1e-11)
    L, S = filters.scale_split(f, mk, 4., sm); ok("large + small = field on wet", ((L+S)-f)[mk > 0], 1e-13); ok("land", S[mk == 0], 0)

large = masked_smooth(field_in, mask, sigma, smooth, smooth_mask)

py-kits › orcakit › filters › scale_split

scale_split

Split a field into a large-scale part and the small-scale residual.

Description

A field is often studied as a resolved part plus what a coarser model cannot see. The large-scale part is masked_smooth of the field and the residual is the rest, so the two add back to the field on valid points.

Both parts are 0 on masked points, as in masked_smooth.

$$f = \tilde f + f',\qquad \tilde f = \text{masked\_smooth}(f),\qquad f' = (f - \tilde f)\,m$$

Syntax

large, small = scale_split(field_in, mask, sigma, smooth)large, small = scale_split(field_in, mask, sigma, smooth, smooth_mask=None)

Input Arguments

field_in — float
Field to split
mask — float
1 for valid points, 0 elsewhere
sigma — float
Filter lengthscale, in gridpoints -- the large/small-scale cutoff
smooth — callable
see masked_smooth
smooth_mask — callable — default None
see masked_smooth

Output Arguments

large — float
Low-pass (large-scale) field, masked
small — float
field_in - large, masked (small-scale residual -- the noise-generating part)

Example

L, S = filters.scale_split(f, mk, 4., sm); ok("large + small = field on wet", ((L+S)-f)[mk > 0], 1e-13); ok("land", S[mk == 0], 0)
Whole test
with test("orcakit.filters.masked_smooth", "orcakit.filters.scale_split"):
    ny, nx = 90, 240; mk = np.ones((ny, nx)); mk[30:50, 60:100] = 0; sm = partial(orca.smooth_2D, mask=None)
    ok("constant stays exact next to land", (filters.masked_smooth(7*mk, mk, 4., sm) - 7)[mk > 0], 1e-11)
    ok("land stays 0", filters.masked_smooth(7*mk, mk, 4., sm)[mk == 0], 0)
    k = 2*np.pi*6/(nx-2); f = np.cos(k*np.arange(nx))[None]*np.ones((ny, nx))
    ok("wave far from land", rerr(filters.masked_smooth(f, np.ones_like(f), 4., sm)[20:-20], (np.exp(-8*k*k)*f)[20:-20]), 2e-3)
    ny7, nx7 = 60, 120; one = np.ones((ny7, nx7)); flip = partial(orca.smooth_2D, mask=None, isMeridional=True); keep = partial(orca.smooth_2D, mask=None)
    ok("a mask of ones gives den = 1 at the fold", filters.masked_smooth(one, one, 4., keep, keep) - 1, 1e-11)
    ok("with smooth_mask, a flipped field leaves den alone", np.abs(filters.masked_smooth(one, one, 4., flip, keep)[-1]).max() - (orca.smooth_2D(one, 4., isMeridional=True)[-1]).max(), 1e-11)
    L, S = filters.scale_split(f, mk, 4., sm); ok("large + small = field on wet", ((L+S)-f)[mk > 0], 1e-13); ok("land", S[mk == 0], 0)

py-kits › orcakit › filters › gaussian

gaussian

Gaussian smoothing in the last two axes of a field that already carries its halo.

Description

This is the plain kernel, with no knowledge of the ORCA seam or fold: it relies on a halo filled beforehand, from the neighbouring tiles or from disk. Pass it as `smooth` to lowpass to filter a padded tile.

Edges are extended with their nearest value, which matters only if the halo is narrower than the kernel, 4 sigma.

$$(G_\sigma * f)_{i,j} = \sum_{m,n} \frac{e^{-(m^2+n^2)/2\sigma^2}}{\sum e^{-(m^2+n^2)/2\sigma^2}}\, f_{i+m,\,j+n}$$

Syntax

field_out = gaussian(field, sigma)

Input Arguments

field — float
(..., ny, nx) padded field
sigma — float
Filter lengthscale, in grid points

Output Arguments

field_out — float
Smoothed field, same shape

Example

Whole test
with test("orcakit.filters.gaussian", "orcakit.filters.lowpass", "orcakit.filters.highpass"):
    from orcakit import filters as FL
    ny_, nx_ = 60, 80; jj, ii = np.mgrid[:ny_, :nx_]; rs = np.random.default_rng(0); f_ = rs.normal(size=(ny_, nx_)); m_ = np.ones((ny_, nx_), bool); m_[20:30, 30:45] = False
    lo = FL.lowpass(f_, m_, 3.); hi = FL.highpass(f_, m_, 3.)
    yes("land is NaN in both", np.isnan(lo[25, 35]) and np.isnan(hi[25, 35]))
    ok("the parts rebuild the field", (lo + hi - f_)[m_], 1e-12)
    ok("constant kept right up to the coast", FL.lowpass(5.*np.ones((ny_, nx_)), m_, 3.)[m_] - 5, 1e-11)
    ok("constant has no high-pass", FL.highpass(5.*np.ones((ny_, nx_)), m_, 3.)[m_], 1e-11)
    from functools import partial
    old = filters.masked_smooth(f_, m_*1., 3., partial(orca.smooth_2D, mask=None))
    ok("same as masked_smooth on wet points", (lo - old)[m_], 1e-12)
    wave = np.sin(2*np.pi*jj/20.)*np.cos(2*np.pi*ii/20.); oo = np.ones_like(m_)
    ok("Gaussian transfer function", (FL.lowpass(wave, oo, 2.) - np.exp(-2*(2*np.pi/20.)**2*2.**2/2)*wave)[12:-12, 12:-12], 5e-3)
    f3 = np.stack([f_, 2*f_]); ok("levels filtered alone, mask broadcast", (FL.lowpass(f3, m_, 3.)[1] - 2*lo)[m_], 1e-12)
    n_ = f_.copy(); n_[5, 5] = np.nan; yes("NaN in the field counts as invalid", np.isnan(FL.lowpass(n_, m_, 3.)[5, 5]) and np.isfinite(FL.lowpass(n_, m_, 3.)[6, 5]))
    isl = np.zeros((ny_, nx_), bool); isl[30, 40] = True; yes("under 1% of the footprint gives NaN", np.isnan(FL.lowpass(f_, isl, 12.)[30, 40]))
    hw = 12; pad = orca.halo(f_, np.array([hw, hw, hw])); wp = orca.halo(m_*1., np.array([hw, hw, hw]))
    pad = np.vstack([np.zeros((hw, pad.shape[1])), pad]); wp = np.vstack([np.zeros((hw, wp.shape[1])), wp])
    out = FL.lowpass(pad, wp > 0, 3., smooth=FL.gaussian); yes("padded tile through `smooth` has the same shape", out.shape == pad.shape)
    ok("tile and whole grid agree in the interior", (out[hw:-hw, hw:-hw] - lo)[hw:-hw, hw:-hw][m_[hw:-hw, hw:-hw]], 1e-9)
    v_ = rs.normal(size=(ny_, nx_)); yes("vector flips at the fold, scalar does not", not np.allclose(FL.lowpass(v_, oo, 3., point="V", vector=True)[-1], FL.lowpass(v_, oo, 3., point="V")[-1]))

py-kits › orcakit › filters › lowpass

lowpass

Gaussian low-pass in space over valid points only, for fields or statistics.

Description

A Gaussian low-pass keeps the scales larger than sigma and removes the rest. On an ocean grid it must ignore land, or every coast is pulled towards zero: the field and the mask of valid points are smoothed with the same kernel and divided. The same call filters a velocity, a mean or a variance; only the sign at the north fold differs.

Where under 1% of the footprint is valid the ratio is not trusted, and the result is NaN there, as on land. By default the ORCA Gaussian handles the seam and the fold; a custom `smooth` can replace it, for example on a tile that already has its halo.

$$\tilde f = \frac{G_\sigma * (f\,m)}{G_\sigma * m} \quad\text{where } m = 1 \text{ and } G_\sigma * m > 0.01,\ \text{else NaN}$$

Syntax

field_out = lowpass(field, mask, sigma)field_out = lowpass(field, mask, sigma, point='T', vector=False, smooth=None)

Input Arguments

field — float
(..., ny, nx); NaN counts as invalid
mask — bool
True where valid, broadcastable to field
sigma — float
Filter lengthscale, in grid points
point — str — default 'T'
'T', 'U', 'V' or 'F', where the field lives
vector — bool — default False
True for a velocity component, which flips sign at the north fold
smooth — callable — default None
smooth(field, sigma); default the ORCA Gaussian (orca.smooth_2D) with this point and sign. The mask is smoothed with it too, so a custom one must not flip sign

Output Arguments

field_out — float
Low-passed field, NaN on invalid points and where under 1% of the footprint was valid

Example

lo = FL.lowpass(f_, m_, 3.); hi = FL.highpass(f_, m_, 3.)
ok("constant kept right up to the coast", FL.lowpass(5.*np.ones((ny_, nx_)), m_, 3.)[m_] - 5, 1e-11)
ok("Gaussian transfer function", (FL.lowpass(wave, oo, 2.) - np.exp(-2*(2*np.pi/20.)**2*2.**2/2)*wave)[12:-12, 12:-12], 5e-3)
f3 = np.stack([f_, 2*f_]); ok("levels filtered alone, mask broadcast", (FL.lowpass(f3, m_, 3.)[1] - 2*lo)[m_], 1e-12)
n_ = f_.copy(); n_[5, 5] = np.nan; yes("NaN in the field counts as invalid", np.isnan(FL.lowpass(n_, m_, 3.)[5, 5]) and np.isfinite(FL.lowpass(n_, m_, 3.)[6, 5]))
isl = np.zeros((ny_, nx_), bool); isl[30, 40] = True; yes("under 1% of the footprint gives NaN", np.isnan(FL.lowpass(f_, isl, 12.)[30, 40]))
out = FL.lowpass(pad, wp > 0, 3., smooth=FL.gaussian); yes("padded tile through `smooth` has the same shape", out.shape == pad.shape)
v_ = rs.normal(size=(ny_, nx_)); yes("vector flips at the fold, scalar does not", not np.allclose(FL.lowpass(v_, oo, 3., point="V", vector=True)[-1], FL.lowpass(v_, oo, 3., point="V")[-1]))

py-kits › orcakit › filters › highpass

highpass

Gaussian high-pass in space, the field minus its low-pass.

Description

The high-pass keeps the scales smaller than sigma, such as eddies and fronts, and is what is left once lowpass has removed the large scales. lowpass and highpass add back to the field on valid points.

It is NaN wherever lowpass is.

$$f' = f - \tilde f,\qquad \tilde f = \text{lowpass}(f)$$

Syntax

field_out = highpass(field, mask, sigma)field_out = highpass(field, mask, sigma, point='T', vector=False, smooth=None)

Input Arguments

field — float
(..., ny, nx); NaN counts as invalid
mask — bool
True where valid, broadcastable to field
sigma — float
Filter lengthscale, in grid points
point — str — default 'T'
'T', 'U', 'V' or 'F', where the field lives
vector — bool — default False
True for a velocity component, which flips sign at the north fold
smooth — callable — default None
See lowpass

Output Arguments

field_out — float
High-passed field, NaN where lowpass is NaN

Example

lo = FL.lowpass(f_, m_, 3.); hi = FL.highpass(f_, m_, 3.)
ok("constant has no high-pass", FL.highpass(5.*np.ones((ny_, nx_)), m_, 3.)[m_], 1e-11)

py-kits › orcakit › filters › lowpass_tile

lowpass_tile

Lowpass on one rank's tile of a domain decomposition.

Description

A whole high-resolution grid with many levels may not fit in one process. Each rank then filters its own tile: a halo of width ceil(4 sigma) is filled from the neighbouring tiles, the padded tile is filtered, and the halo is stripped, which gives the same result as filtering the whole grid.

With a serial decomposition it filters the whole grid. The halo, plus 5 rows for the fold, must fit in the smallest tile.

$$\tilde f = \frac{G_\sigma * (f\,m)}{G_\sigma * m} \text{ on the tile, with a halo of } \lceil 4\sigma \rceil \text{ from the neighbours}$$

Syntax

field_out = lowpass_tile(dec, field, mask, sigma)field_out = lowpass_tile(dec, field, mask, sigma, point='T', vector=False)

Input Arguments

dec — Decomp
mpi_orca decomposition; 4 sigma + 5 must fit in its smallest tile
field — float
(..., jl, il) this rank's tile; NaN counts as invalid
mask — bool
True where valid, (jl, il) or the shape of field
sigma — float
Filter lengthscale, in grid points
point — str — default 'T'
'T', 'U', 'V' or 'F', where the field lives
vector — bool — default False
True for a velocity component, which flips sign at the north fold

Output Arguments

field_out — float
(..., jl, il) low-passed tile, NaN as in lowpass

Example

t_lp = filters.lowpass_tile(dec_, f_, m_, 3., point="U", vector=True); yes("interior shape kept", t_lp.shape == f_.shape); yes("land is NaN", np.isnan(t_lp[25, 35]))
ok("constant kept to the coast", filters.lowpass_tile(dec_, 5*np.ones((ny_, nx_), np.float32), m_, 3.)[m_] - 5, 2e-5)
Whole test

    ny_, nx_ = 60, 80; dec_ = mo.Decomp.serial_decomp(ny_, nx_); f_ = np.random.default_rng(3).normal(size=(ny_, nx_)).astype(np.float32); m_ = np.ones((ny_, nx_), bool); m_[20:30, 30:45] = False
    t_lp = filters.lowpass_tile(dec_, f_, m_, 3., point="U", vector=True); yes("interior shape kept", t_lp.shape == f_.shape); yes("land is NaN", np.isnan(t_lp[25, 35]))
    ok("same as the whole-grid lowpass away from the south edge", (t_lp - filters.lowpass(f_, m_, 3., point="U", vector=True))[15:][m_[15:]], 2e-5)
    ok("constant kept to the coast", filters.lowpass_tile(dec_, 5*np.ones((ny_, nx_), np.float32), m_, 3.)[m_] - 5, 2e-5)
    yes("serial gather returns the field", mo.gather(dec_, f_, root=0) is f_)

py-kits › orcakit › filters › deseason

deseason

Remove, point by point, the mean, a linear trend and the harmonics of a period.

Description

The seasonal cycle and a slow drift often dominate a record but are not the variability of interest. This fits them by least squares at every point and returns what is left. Unlike a broad high-pass in time, it removes only those components and leaves every other time scale as it was.

All points are fitted in one small least-squares system. A point with any NaN in time stays NaN. The record must be longer than the number of coefficients, and a few years are needed to separate the trend from the seasons.

$$f(t) \approx a_0 + a_1\,\frac{t - t_0}{t_{\mathrm{end}} - t_0} + \sum_{k=1}^{K} \big[b_k \cos(k\omega t) + c_k \sin(k\omega t)\big],\qquad \omega = \frac{2\pi}{P}$$
$$\text{residual} = f - \text{fit, by least squares at each point}$$

Syntax

residual, coef = deseason(field, time_days)residual, coef = deseason(field, time_days, harmonics=2, period=365.25)

Input Arguments

field — float
(nt, ...) record
time_days — float
(nt,) time, in days
harmonics — int — default 2
Number of harmonics; 2 for annual and semiannual
period — float — default 365.25
Period, in days

Output Arguments

residual — float
(nt, ...) field minus the fit
coef — float
(2 + 2*harmonics, ...) mean, trend over the record, then the cosine and sine of each harmonic. Raises ValueError if nt is too short for them

Example

r_, co = FL.deseason(fld, t_)
FL.deseason(fld[:4], t_[:4]); yes("too few snapshots refused", False)
Whole test
with test("orcakit.filters.deseason", "orcakit.filters.time_lowpass"):
    t_ = np.arange(0., 1095.); om = 2*np.pi/365.25; noise_ = np.random.default_rng(1).normal(size=(t_.size, 4, 5))*0.01
    sea = 3 + 2*(t_/t_[-1]) + np.cos(om*t_) + 0.5*np.sin(2*om*t_)
    fld = sea[:, None, None] + noise_; fld[:, 0, 0] = np.nan
    r_, co = FL.deseason(fld, t_)
    yes("residual is about the noise", np.nanstd(r_) < 0.011 and abs(np.nanstd(r_) - 0.01) < 1e-3)
    ok("annual amplitude recovered", co[2, 1, 1] - 1, 5e-3); ok("semiannual amplitude recovered", co[5, 1, 1] - 0.5, 5e-3)
    yes("a NaN stays NaN", np.isnan(r_[:, 0, 0]).all())
    try:
        FL.deseason(fld[:4], t_[:4]); yes("too few snapshots refused", False)
    except ValueError:
        yes("too few snapshots refused", True)
    slow, fast = np.sin(2*np.pi*t_/200.), np.sin(2*np.pi*t_/5.)
    lp = FL.time_lowpass((slow + fast)[:, None]*np.ones((1, 3)), 1., 30.)
    ok("slow signal kept, fast removed, away from the ends", (lp[:, 1] - slow)[100:-100], 2e-3)
    b_ = np.ones((t_.size, 2)); b_[3, 0] = np.nan; yes("Butterworth leaves NaN columns as NaN", np.isnan(FL.time_lowpass(b_, 1., 30.)[:, 0]).all())

Result in tests/test_all_routines.ipynb:

PASS  annual amplitude recovered: 1.935e-04 (tol 5.0e-03)
PASS  semiannual amplitude recovered: 5.230e-04 (tol 5.0e-03)
PASS  a NaN stays NaN
PASS  too few snapshots refused
PASS  slow signal kept, fast removed, away from the ends: 5.519e-04 (tol 2.0e-03)
PASS  Butterworth leaves NaN columns as NaN

py-kits › orcakit › filters › time_lowpass

time_lowpass

Zero-phase Butterworth low-pass in time, along axis 0.

Description

A Butterworth filter has a flat response below its cutoff and falls off quickly above it. Run forward and then backward, it shifts no event in time, which matters when a filtered series is compared with the original. The high-pass is the field minus the result.

The start and end of the record are less reliable, since the filter needs data on both sides. A point with any NaN in time stays NaN.

$$|H(\omega)|^2 = \Big[1 + (\omega/\omega_c)^{2N}\Big]^{-1},\qquad \omega_c = \frac{2\pi}{T_c}$$
$$\text{applied forward and backward, so the gain is } |H|^2 \text{ and there is no phase shift}$$

Syntax

field_out = time_lowpass(field, dt, cutoff_period)field_out = time_lowpass(field, dt, cutoff_period, order=5)

Input Arguments

field — float
(nt, ...) record; points with any NaN in time stay NaN
dt — float
Time between snapshots
cutoff_period — float
Shortest period kept, in the unit of dt
order — int — default 5
Order of the filter

Output Arguments

field_out — float
(nt, ...) low-passed record

Example

lp = FL.time_lowpass((slow + fast)[:, None]*np.ones((1, 3)), 1., 30.)
b_ = np.ones((t_.size, 2)); b_[3, 0] = np.nan; yes("Butterworth leaves NaN columns as NaN", np.isnan(FL.time_lowpass(b_, 1., 30.)[:, 0]).all())

py-kits › orcakit

grid_c

Arakawa C-grid interpolation, differentiation, divergence and vorticity operators. These are grid-generic: every operator that needs boundary padding takes an `exchange` callable rather than importing one, so this module has no dependency on any specific grid family (e.g. ORCA's tripolar north-fold). Pass `orca.halo` (see orca.py) for ORCA-family grids.

exchange signature: exchange(field, halo_array, isMeridional=False, point="T") -> haloed_field

The north fold flips the sign of both velocity components, and its mapping depends on the grid point (T, U, V or F).

Functions

ke_computeSum of the squares of the four velocities around each interior T-point.
uv2tSum of the four velocities around each interior T-point.
interp_UV2TAverage a U-point or V-point field onto T-points.
interp_T2UVAverage a T-point field onto U-points or V-points.
interp_1DAverage a field with its next neighbour along x or along y.
fdiff_1DForward difference along x or along y, divided by a scale factor.
bdiff_1DBackward difference along x or along y, divided by a scale factor.
dxFu_1DThe zonal part of a flux divergence on T-points.
hDiv_VgridHorizontal divergence on T-points of velocities on U-points and V-points.
w_from_divergenceVertical velocity by integrating the divergence up from the bottom.
vertical_velocityVertical velocity from horizontal velocity, by continuity, as NEMO computes it.
geostrophic_uvSurface geostrophic velocity from sea surface height.
geostrophic_uv.corner_sumSum of each 2 x 2 block, the four T-points around an F-point.
hDiv_TgridHorizontal divergence on T-points of velocities that are themselves on T-points.
vort_VgridRelative vorticity on F-points of velocities on U-points and V-points.
py-kits › orcakit › grid_c › ke_compute

ke_compute

Sum of the squares of the four velocities around each interior T-point.

Description

Kinetic energy is defined at T-points, but on the C grid the velocities are on the faces. Summing the squares of the two U-points and two V-points around each T-point puts it there.

The result is 4 times the kinetic energy, kept for older callers; diagkit.stats.kinetic_energy returns the energy itself. The outer rows and columns are 0.

$$K_{i,j} = u_{i-1,j}^2 + u_{i,j}^2 + v_{i,j-1}^2 + v_{i,j}^2$$

Syntax

ke = ke_compute(u, v)

Input Arguments

u — float
(..., ny, nx) U-point velocity
v — float
(..., ny, nx) V-point velocity

Output Arguments

ke — float
(..., ny, nx) u(i-1)^2 + u(i)^2 + v(j-1)^2 + v(j)^2 on interior T-points, 0 on the outer rows and columns

Example

ok("ke_compute interior", grid_c.ke_compute(u, v)[1:-1, 1:-1] - 50, 1e-13)
Whole test
with test("orcakit.grid_c.ke_compute", "orcakit.grid_c.uv2t"):
    u, v = 3*np.ones((6, 7)), 4*np.ones((6, 7))
    ok("ke_compute interior", grid_c.ke_compute(u, v)[1:-1, 1:-1] - 50, 1e-13)
    ok("uv2t interior", grid_c.uv2t(u, v)[1:-1, 1:-1] - 14, 1e-13)

uv2t

$$S_{i,j} = u_{i-1,j} + u_{i,j} + v_{i,j-1} + v_{i,j}$$

(..., ny, nx) U-point velocity
v — float

(..., ny, nx) u(i-1) + u(i) + v(j-1) + v(j) on interior T-points, 0 on the outer rows and columns

py-kits › orcakit › grid_c › interp_UV2T

interp_UV2T

Average a U-point or V-point field onto T-points.

Description

On the C grid, u sits on the east face of each cell and v on its north face, so the two components, and anything computed from both, are never at the same place. Products such as u v, kinetic energy or the covariance of u and v need them co-located first: this averages the two faces on either side of each T-point, along x for U fields and along y for V fields.

Along x the western neighbour of column 0 comes from the periodic seam, through exchange. Along y, row 0 has no V-point below it and keeps V(0); on the ORCA grids that row is land. With weights, the average is weighted, e.g. by face areas e2u e3u to average transports.

$$\overline{u}^{\,i}_{i,j} = \tfrac12\,(u_{i-1,j} + u_{i,j}),\qquad \overline{v}^{\,j}_{i,j} = \tfrac12\,(v_{i,j-1} + v_{i,j})$$
$$\text{with weights: } \overline{u}^{\,i}_{i,j} = \frac{w_{i-1,j}\,u_{i-1,j} + w_{i,j}\,u_{i,j}}{w_{i-1,j} + w_{i,j}}$$

Syntax

field_out = interp_UV2T(field_in, exchange)field_out = interp_UV2T(field_in, exchange, weights_in=None, dir=None, isMeridional=False)

Input Arguments

field_in — float
(..., ny, nx) field on U-points (dir='lon') or V-points (dir='lat')
exchange — callable
Boundary/halo exchange, e.g. orca.halo
weights_in — float — default None
Weights at the same points, same shape, or None for a plain mean
dir — str — default None
'lon' for U to T, 'lat' for V to T
isMeridional — bool — default False
Unused: neither direction reads across the north fold

Output Arguments

field_out — float
(..., ny, nx) field on T-points

Example

ok("UV2T lon linear", rerr(grid_c.interp_UV2T(f, orca.halo, dir="lon")[:, 1:], (f - 1.0)[:, 1:]), 1e-14)
ok("UV2T lat linear", rerr(grid_c.interp_UV2T(f, orca.halo, dir="lat")[1:], (f - 1.5)[1:]), 1e-14)
ok("UV2T lon weighted, constant", rerr(grid_c.interp_UV2T(0*f+7, orca.halo, weights_in=w, dir="lon"), 7.), 1e-14)
ok("UV2T lat weighted, constant", rerr(grid_c.interp_UV2T(0*f+7, orca.halo, weights_in=w, dir="lat"), 7.), 1e-14)
Whole test
with test("orcakit.grid_c.interp_T2UV", "orcakit.grid_c.interp_1D", "orcakit.grid_c.interp_UV2T"):
    ny, nx = 8, 12; jj, ii = np.mgrid[:ny, :nx].astype(float); f = 3*jj + 2*ii + 1; w = 1 + (jj+ii) % 3
    for name, fn in (("T2UV", grid_c.interp_T2UV), ("1D", grid_c.interp_1D)):
        ok(f"{name} lon linear", rerr(fn(f, orca.halo, dir="lon")[:, :-1], (f + 1.0)[:, :-1]), 1e-14)
        ok(f"{name} lat linear", rerr(fn(f, orca.halo, dir="lat")[:-1], (f + 1.5)[:-1]), 1e-14)
        ok(f"{name} lon weighted, constant stays", rerr(fn(0*f+7, orca.halo, weights_in=w, dir="lon"), 7.), 1e-14)
        h = (w[:, :-1]*f[:, :-1] + w[:, 1:]*f[:, 1:])/(w[:, :-1]+w[:, 1:])
        ok(f"{name} lon weighted, hand value", rerr(fn(f, orca.halo, weights_in=w, dir="lon")[:, :-1], h), 1e-14)
        h = (w[:-1]*f[:-1] + w[1:]*f[1:])/(w[:-1]+w[1:])
        ok(f"{name} lat weighted, hand value", rerr(fn(f, orca.halo, weights_in=w, dir="lat")[:-1], h), 1e-14)
    ok("UV2T lon linear", rerr(grid_c.interp_UV2T(f, orca.halo, dir="lon")[:, 1:], (f - 1.0)[:, 1:]), 1e-14)
    ok("UV2T lat linear", rerr(grid_c.interp_UV2T(f, orca.halo, dir="lat")[1:], (f - 1.5)[1:]), 1e-14)
    ok("UV2T lon weighted, constant", rerr(grid_c.interp_UV2T(0*f+7, orca.halo, weights_in=w, dir="lon"), 7.), 1e-14)
    ok("UV2T lat weighted, constant", rerr(grid_c.interp_UV2T(0*f+7, orca.halo, weights_in=w, dir="lat"), 7.), 1e-14)

py-kits › orcakit › grid_c › interp_T2UV

interp_T2UV

Average a T-point field onto U-points or V-points.

Description

Tracers, sea level and cell thicknesses live at the centre of the cells, but terms of the momentum or transport budgets are needed on the faces, next to the velocities. This averages the two T-points on either side of each face, along x for U-points and along y for V-points.

The neighbour beyond the last column or row comes from the halo: the periodic seam in x, the north fold in y, where isMeridional flips the sign for a velocity component. With weights, the average is weighted.

$$\overline{T}^{\,i}_{i,j} = \tfrac12\,(T_{i,j} + T_{i+1,j}),\qquad \overline{T}^{\,j}_{i,j} = \tfrac12\,(T_{i,j} + T_{i,j+1})$$

Syntax

field_out = interp_T2UV(field_in, exchange)field_out = interp_T2UV(field_in, exchange, weights_in=None, dir=None, isMeridional=False)

Input Arguments

field_in — float
Field to be interpolated
exchange — callable
Boundary/halo exchange, see module docstring
weights_in — float — default None
Interpolation weights
dir — str — default None
Direction of interpolation, 'lon' or 'lat'
isMeridional — bool — default False
if True, change the sign of the north halo

Output Arguments

field_out — float
Resulting field

Example

    ny, nx = 8, 12; jj, ii = np.mgrid[:ny, :nx].astype(float); f = 3*jj + 2*ii + 1; w = 1 + (jj+ii) % 3
    for name, fn in (("T2UV", grid_c.interp_T2UV), ("1D", grid_c.interp_1D)):
        ok(f"{name} lon linear", rerr(fn(f, orca.halo, dir="lon")[:, :-1], (f + 1.0)[:, :-1]), 1e-14)
        ok(f"{name} lat linear", rerr(fn(f, orca.halo, dir="lat")[:-1], (f + 1.5)[:-1]), 1e-14)
        ok(f"{name} lon weighted, constant stays", rerr(fn(0*f+7, orca.halo, weights_in=w, dir="lon"), 7.), 1e-14)
        h = (w[:, :-1]*f[:, :-1] + w[:, 1:]*f[:, 1:])/(w[:, :-1]+w[:, 1:])
        ok(f"{name} lon weighted, hand value", rerr(fn(f, orca.halo, weights_in=w, dir="lon")[:, :-1], h), 1e-14)
        h = (w[:-1]*f[:-1] + w[1:]*f[1:])/(w[:-1]+w[1:])
        ok(f"{name} lat weighted, hand value", rerr(fn(f, orca.halo, weights_in=w, dir="lat")[:-1], h), 1e-14)
    ok("UV2T lon linear", rerr(grid_c.interp_UV2T(f, orca.halo, dir="lon")[:, 1:], (f - 1.0)[:, 1:]), 1e-14)

py-kits › orcakit › grid_c › interp_1D

interp_1D

Average a field with its next neighbour along x or along y.

Description

The general form of interp_T2UV for any C-grid point: each value is averaged with the one after it, so a field moves half a cell forward, for example from U-points to F-points along y.

The neighbour after the last column or row comes from the halo, with the fold rule of `point` and the sign flip given by isMeridional. With weights, the average is weighted.

$$\overline{f}^{\,i}_{i,j} = \tfrac12\,(f_{i,j} + f_{i+1,j}),\qquad \overline{f}^{\,j}_{i,j} = \tfrac12\,(f_{i,j} + f_{i,j+1})$$

Syntax

field_out = interp_1D(field_in, exchange)field_out = interp_1D(field_in, exchange, weights_in=None, dir=None, isMeridional=False, point='T')

Input Arguments

field_in — float
Field to be interpolated
exchange — callable
Boundary/halo exchange, see module docstring
weights_in — float — default None
Interpolation weights
dir — str — default None
Direction of interpolation, 'lon' or 'lat'
isMeridional — bool — default False
if True, change the sign of the north halo
point — str — default 'T'
Where field_in lives, 'T', 'U', 'V' or 'F'

Output Arguments

field_out — float
Resulting field

Example
