py-kits › modredkit › dmd › exactDMD

exactDMD

Exact dynamic mode decomposition of pairs of snapshots.

Description

DMD finds spatial modes that each evolve with one complex frequency and growth rate, from snapshots one time step apart: the best linear map from each snapshot to the next, reduced to the rank of the truncated SVD.

$$X_b = U S V^{*},\qquad \tilde A = U^{*} X_a V S^{-1},\qquad \tilde A W = W \Lambda,\qquad \Phi = X_a V S^{-1} W$$

Syntax

dmd_mds, dt_eig, ns, U, S, Vh, W = exactDMD(Xb, Xa, r)dmd_mds, dt_eig, ns, U, S, Vh, W = exactDMD(Xb, Xa, r, SVD_out=False, verbose=False)

Input Arguments

Xb — float
(n, m) snapshots before, one per column
Xa — float
(n, m) the same snapshots one step later
r — int/float
Rank of the SVD, or share of information to keep
SVD_out — bool — default False
Also return the SVD and the eigenvectors of A~
verbose — bool — default False
Print the shapes

Output Arguments

dmd_mds — complex
(n, r) DMD modes
dt_eig — complex
(r,) discrete-time eigenvalues
ns — int
Number of modes
U, S, Vh — float
The SVD of Xb, with SVD_out only
W — complex
(r, r) eigenvectors of A~, with SVD_out only

Example

mds, ev, nm = D.exactDMD(Xb, Xa, 5); ok("eigenvalues", match(LAM, ev), 1e-10); yes("5 modes", nm == 5)

py-kits › modredkit › dmd › kernelDMD

kernelDMD

Kernel dynamic mode decomposition from a Gram matrix (Williams, Rowley and Kevrekidis 2015).

Description

Kernel DMD works with the inner products of the snapshots rather than the snapshots themselves, and a nonlinear kernel lets it approximate the Koopman operator of nonlinear dynamics with modest cost.

The Gram matrix of all snapshots gives G~ (pairs before) and A~ (pairs after); the eigendecomposition of G~, truncated to r, yields the Koopman approximation, whose eigenvalues and modes are returned.

$$\tilde G = Q \Sigma^2 Q^{T},\qquad \hat K = (\Sigma^{+} Q^{T})\, \tilde A\, (Q \Sigma^{+}),\qquad \hat K V = V M,\qquad \lambda^{c} = \frac{\log \mu}{\Delta t}$$

Syntax

kDMD_mds, ct_eig, mu, A, Vr, nx, nm = kernelDMD(S2, X, dt, r)kDMD_mds, ct_eig, mu, A, Vr, nx, nm = kernelDMD(S2, X, dt, r, Y=None, verbose=False, noModes=False)

Input Arguments

S2 — float
(nt, nt) Gram matrix k(x_i, x_j) of all snapshots
X — float
(nt-1, n) snapshots before, one per row, to project the modes on
dt — float
Time between snapshots
r — int
Rank kept from the eigendecomposition of G~
Y — float — default None
Unused
verbose — bool — default False
Unused
noModes — bool — default False
Return only the eigenvalues

Output Arguments

kDMD_mds — complex
(n, r) Koopman modes, None with noModes
ct_eig — complex
(r,) continuous-time eigenvalues, log(mu)/dt
mu — complex
(r,) discrete-time eigenvalues
A — complex
(nt-1, r) Q Sigma^+ V, None with noModes
Vr — complex
(r, r) right eigenvectors of K, None with noModes
nx — int
Rows of Phi = Q Sigma V, None with noModes
nm — int
Number of modes, None with noModes

Example

G = SNAP.T @ SNAP; out = D.kernelDMD(G, SNAP[:, :-1].T, dt, 5); ok("linear kernel eigenvalues", match(LAM, out[2]), 1e-7); ok("continuous", match(np.log(LAM)/dt, out[1]), 1e-7)
Z = np.array(xs).T; Gp = Mo.gram(Z, "poly", 2, 1.); ev = D.kernelDMD(Gp, Z[:, :-1].T, 1., 6, noModes=True)[2]
Gl = Z.T@Z; ml, ctl, evl, *_ = D.kernelDMD(Gl, Z[:, :-1].T, 1., 2)

    for _ in range(60): xs.append(R@xs[-1])
    Z = np.array(xs).T; Gp = Mo.gram(Z, "poly", 2, 1.); ev = D.kernelDMD(Gp, Z[:, :-1].T, 1., 6, noModes=True)[2]
    ex = np.array([1, rho*np.exp(1j*th), rho*np.exp(-1j*th), rho**2*np.exp(2j*th), rho**2*np.exp(-2j*th), rho**2])
    ok("polynomial kernel: closed-form Koopman eigenvalues", match(ex, ev), 1e-6)
    Gl = Z.T@Z; ml, ctl, evl, *_ = D.kernelDMD(Gl, Z[:, :-1].T, 1., 2)
    bb = np.linalg.lstsq(ml, Z[:, 0], rcond=None)[0]; ok("modes span the data: rebuild", ((ml*bb)@(evl[:, None]**np.arange(40)[None])).real - Z[:, :40], 1e-6)

DMD_continuous_eig

Continuous-time eigenvalues from discrete-time ones.

Description

Discrete eigenvalues depend on the time step; continuous ones give the growth rate (real part) and angular frequency (imaginary part) in physical units.

$$\lambda^{c} = \frac{\log \lambda}{\Delta t}$$

Syntax

ct_eig = DMD_continuous_eig(dt_eig, dt)

Input Arguments

dt_eig — complex
Discrete-time eigenvalues
dt — float
Time between snapshots

Output Arguments

ct_eig — complex
Continuous-time eigenvalues; real part the growth rate, imaginary part the angular frequency

Example

ct = D.DMD_continuous_eig(np.array([np.exp(.6j)*.5]), dt); ok("mu = ln(lambda)/dt", ct - (np.log(.5)+.6j)/dt, 1e-14)
Whole test
with test("modredkit.dmd.exactDMD", "modredkit.dmd.exactDMD_Light", "modredkit.dmd.DefineXandXp", "modredkit.dmd.DMD_continuous_eig"):
    Xb, Xa = D.DefineXandXp(SNAP); ok("X and X' shifted", Xb[:, 1:] - Xa[:, :-1], 0)
    mds, ev, nm = D.exactDMD(Xb, Xa, 5); ok("eigenvalues", match(LAM, ev), 1e-10); yes("5 modes", nm == 5)
    i = np.argmin(np.abs(ev - LAM[0])); ok("mode parallel to phi_1", 1 - np.abs(np.vdot(mds[:, i], ph1))/(np.linalg.norm(mds[:, i])*np.linalg.norm(ph1)), 1e-10)
    ok("Light gives the same eigenvalues", match(LAM, D.exactDMD_Light(SNAP, 5)[1]), 1e-10)
    ct = D.DMD_continuous_eig(np.array([np.exp(.6j)*.5]), dt); ok("mu = ln(lambda)/dt", ct - (np.log(.5)+.6j)/dt, 1e-14)

py-kits › modredkit › dmd › getConjugatePairsMask

getConjugatePairsMask

Keep one eigenvalue of each complex-conjugate pair.

Description

For a real field, modes come in conjugate pairs that carry the same information. Keeping the one with Im >= 0, and every real mode, halves the storage, which is how NEMO's noise input stores them.

$$\text{keep } k \iff \mathrm{Im}\,\lambda_k \ge 0$$

Syntax

mask, nm_out = getConjugatePairsMask(ct_eig)

Input Arguments

ct_eig — complex
Eigenvalues

Output Arguments

mask — bool
True for the eigenvalues kept
nm_out — int
Number kept

Example

mk, nn = D.getConjugatePairsMask(np.array([1+2j, 1-2j, .1+0j, .2+0j])); ok("pair kept once, both real modes kept", nn - 3, 0); yes("the kept pair member has Im > 0", mk[0] and not mk[1])
Whole test

DMD_amplitudes_2014Jovanovich

Optimal amplitudes of Jovanovic et al. (2014), computed from the SVD.

Description

The amplitudes do not change under the rotation of the SVD, so the global least-squares problem of DMD_amplitudes_optimal is solved in SVD coordinates, which is cheaper. An earlier version built a square Vandermonde matrix and was right only without truncation.

$$b = \arg\min_b \big\| S V^{*} - W\, \mathrm{diag}(b)\, \mathrm{Vand}(\lambda) \big\|_F$$

S — float
(r,) singular values of the snapshots before
V — float
(m, r) right singular vectors, Vh.conj().T; (r, m) is also accepted
W — complex
(r, r) eigenvectors of the reduced operator A~
dt_eig — complex
(r,) discrete-time eigenvalues

Output Arguments

amp — complex
(r,) amplitudes

py-kits › modredkit › dmd › DMD_amplitudes_optimal

DMD_amplitudes_optimal

Amplitudes that fit the whole record, not only its first snapshot.

Description

Fitting one snapshot leaves the amplitudes at the mercy of that snapshot's noise. This minimises the misfit over all snapshots at once (Jovanovic et al. 2014), from the modes and eigenvalues alone, so it suits both exactDMD and kernelDMD. Fit the same field the modes describe.

$$b = \arg\min_b \| X - \Phi\, \mathrm{diag}(b)\, \mathrm{Vand} \|_F,\qquad P b = q,\quad P = (\Phi^{*}\Phi) \circ \overline{\mathrm{Vand}\,\mathrm{Vand}^{*}},\quad q = \mathrm{diag}(\Phi^{*} X\, \mathrm{Vand}^{*})$$

Syntax

b, energy = DMD_amplitudes_optimal(dmd_mds, dt_eig, X)b, energy = DMD_amplitudes_optimal(dmd_mds, dt_eig, X, return_energy=False)

Input Arguments

dmd_mds — complex
(n, r) modes, one per column
dt_eig — complex
(r,) discrete-time eigenvalues
X — float
(n, m) snapshots to fit, X[:, j] ~ Phi diag(b) dt_eig^j
return_energy — bool — default False
Also return each mode's contribution

Output Arguments

b — complex
(r,) amplitudes
energy — float
(r,) |b_k| ||Phi_k|| ||dt_eig_k^j||, to rank modes; with return_energy only

Example

py-kits › modredkit › dmd › ShiftStack

ShiftStack

Stack time-shifted copies of the snapshots, a delay embedding.

Description

Stacking delayed copies lets DMD represent dynamics that one snapshot alone cannot, such as standing oscillations or a few dominant frequencies in a small state.

$$\begin{pmatrix} S_{:,0:m-s} \\ S_{:,1:m-s+1} \\ \vdots \\ S_{:,s:m} \end{pmatrix}$$

Syntax

ssS = ShiftStack(S, m, s)

Input Arguments

S — float
(n, m) snapshots, one per column
m — int
Number of snapshots
s — int
Number of shifted copies added

Output Arguments

ssS — float
((s+1) n, m-s) S[:, :m-s] stacked over S[:, i+1:m-s+i+1], i = 0 .. s-1

Example

Sx = np.arange(1., 7.)[None]; ss = D.ShiftStack(Sx, 6, 2); ok("Hankel rows", ss - [[1, 2, 3, 4], [2, 3, 4, 5], [3, 4, 5, 6]], 0)
yy = np.cos(.4*np.arange(40.))[None]; hh = D.ShiftStack(yy, 40, 5); ok("delay embedding finds omega for a scalar", match(np.exp([.4j, -.4j]), D.exactDMD(hh[:, :-1], hh[:, 1:], 2)[1]), 1e-10)
Whole test
with test("modredkit.dmd.RemGtT", "modredkit.dmd.CleanUnitCircle", "modredkit.dmd.SortByFrequency", "modredkit.dmd.ShiftStack"):
    lam = np.array([1.0, .95, 1.2]); ct = np.log(lam.astype(complex)); ph = np.eye(3); am = np.array([1., 2., 3.])
    out = D.RemGtT(ph, lam, ct, am); ok("RemGtT default drops only the growing mode", out[3] - [1., 2.], 0)
    ok("RemGtT threshold honoured: 0.96 keeps only 0.95", D.RemGtT(ph, lam, ct, am, treshold=.96)[3] - [2.], 0)
    out = D.CleanUnitCircle(ph, ct, lam, am, .1); ok("CleanUnitCircle", out[3] - [1., 2.], 0); ok("count", out[4] - 2, 0)
    ct2 = np.array([-10+.1j, 0+1j]); s = D.SortByFrequency(np.eye(2), ct2, ct2, ct2); ok("sorted by |Im mu|", s[1].imag - [.1, 1], 0)
    Sx = np.arange(1., 7.)[None]; ss = D.ShiftStack(Sx, 6, 2); ok("Hankel rows", ss - [[1, 2, 3, 4], [2, 3, 4, 5], [3, 4, 5, 6]], 0)
    yy = np.cos(.4*np.arange(40.))[None]; hh = D.ShiftStack(yy, 40, 5); ok("delay embedding finds omega for a scalar", match(np.exp([.4j, -.4j]), D.exactDMD(hh[:, :-1], hh[:, 1:], 2)[1]), 1e-10)

Reshape a space-time array into a matrix with space in rows and time in columns.

Input Arguments

shape — bool — default False
Also return the sizes needed to undo it
verbose — bool — default False
Print shapes

Output Arguments

(nz*ny*nx, nt) matrix
nt — int
Number of snapshots, with shape only
ns — tuple
Spatial shape, with shape only

Example

Whole test

py-kits › modredkit › dmd › mrDMD

mrDMD

Windowed multi-level DMD.

Description

Level l splits the record into 2^l windows and runs exactDMD on each, so slow modes come from the long windows and fast ones from the short. Growing modes are dropped and amplitudes fit each window's first snapshot.

Unlike the full mrDMD of Kutz et al. (2016), slow modes are not subtracted between levels and the data are not subsampled. A remainder after the last whole window is dropped.

$$\text{for } l = 0..L-1,\ j = 0..2^l-1:\quad \text{exactDMD}\big(X_{:,\ j s:(j+1) s}\big),\qquad s = \lfloor m / 2^l \rfloor$$

Syntax

out_mds, out_dt, out_ct, out_amp, out_idx = mrDMD(Xraw, r, dt, L)

Input Arguments

Xraw — float
(n, m) snapshots, one per column
r — int
Rank of each window's SVD
dt — float
Time between snapshots
L — int
Number of levels

Output Arguments

out_mds — complex
(n, K) modes of all windows, one per column
out_dt — complex
(K,) discrete-time eigenvalues
out_ct — complex
(K,) continuous-time eigenvalues
out_amp — complex
(K,) amplitudes
out_idx — int
(K, 3) level, window and mode of each column

Example

mds, ldt, lct, amp, idx = D.mrDMD(Xo, 2, 1., 3); yes("seven windows", len({(a, b) for a, b, _ in idx}) == 7); yes("2 modes per window", idx.shape[0] == 14)
Xd = Q[:, 0:1]*.9**t; yes("damped mode kept", D.mrDMD(Xd, 1, 1., 1)[1].size == 1)
Xg = Q[:, 0:1]*1.05**t; yes("growing mode dropped", D.mrDMD(Xg, 1, 1., 1)[1].size == 0)
Whole test
with test("modredkit.dmd.mrDMD"):
    n, m = 40, 160; Q, _ = np.linalg.qr(np.random.default_rng(6).standard_normal((n, 3))); t = np.arange(m)
    Xo = Q[:, 0:1]*np.cos(.5*t) + Q[:, 1:2]*np.sin(.5*t)
    mds, ldt, lct, amp, idx = D.mrDMD(Xo, 2, 1., 3); yes("seven windows", len({(a, b) for a, b, _ in idx}) == 7); yes("2 modes per window", idx.shape[0] == 14)
    ok("lambda in all windows", np.abs(np.abs(ldt.imag) - np.sin(.5)).max(), 1e-10); ok("omega", np.abs(lct.imag) - .5, 1e-10)
    Xd = Q[:, 0:1]*.9**t; yes("damped mode kept", D.mrDMD(Xd, 1, 1., 1)[1].size == 1)
    Xg = Q[:, 0:1]*1.05**t; yes("growing mode dropped", D.mrDMD(Xg, 1, 1., 1)[1].size == 0)

py-kits › modredkit

modes

Working with snapshot matrices and modes. Snapshot matrices are (n, m) and modes (n, r), as in dmd.py. Selectors return a boolean mask over modes, applied with apply_mask, so that they combine with & and |.

Functions

packStack the wet points of several fields into one snapshot matrix.
unpackThe inverse of pack, for snapshots or modes.
gramThe snapshot kernel matrix for kernel DMD.
mask_unit_circleThe modes near the unit circle, neither growing nor decaying much.
mask_not_growingThe modes that do not grow.
mask_periodThe modes whose period lies in a range.
mask_one_per_pairOne mode of each complex-conjugate pair; real modes are all kept.
mask_top_energyThe n modes that contribute most to the record.
apply_maskKeep the selected modes, in the modes and in any per-mode arrays.
time_dynamicsThe time behaviour of each mode over a number of snapshots.
reconstructThe real snapshot matrix from modes, amplitudes and eigenvalues.
py-kits › modredkit › modes › pack

pack

Stack the wet points of several fields into one snapshot matrix.

Description

Decompositions want one column per snapshot and no land. Several fields, such as u and v, can share the matrix, so their joint variability is decomposed.

$$X = \begin{pmatrix} f^{(1)}[w^{(1)}] \\ f^{(2)}[w^{(2)}] \\ \vdots \end{pmatrix},\ \text{one column per snapshot}$$

Syntax

X = pack(fields, wets)

Input Arguments

fields — list
(m, ...) arrays, m snapshots each
wets — list
Wet mask of each field, its shape without the first axis

Output Arguments

X — float
(n, m) matrix, the wet points of each field in turn, one snapshot per column

Example

f = np.arange(24.).reshape(4, 2, 3); wet = np.array([[1, 1, 0], [0, 1, 1]], bool); g = 2*f; X = Mo.pack([f, g], [wet, wet]); yes("shape", X.shape == (8, 4))
Whole test
with test("modredkit.modes.pack", "modredkit.modes.unpack", "modredkit.modes.gram", "modredkit.modes.mask_unit_circle", "modredkit.modes.mask_not_growing", "modredkit.modes.mask_period", "modredkit.modes.mask_one_per_pair", "modredkit.modes.mask_top_energy", "modredkit.modes.apply_mask", "modredkit.modes.time_dynamics", "modredkit.modes.reconstruct"):
    f = np.arange(24.).reshape(4, 2, 3); wet = np.array([[1, 1, 0], [0, 1, 1]], bool); g = 2*f; X = Mo.pack([f, g], [wet, wet]); yes("shape", X.shape == (8, 4))
    a, b = Mo.unpack(X, [wet, wet]); ok("field", a[:, wet] - f[:, wet], 0); yes("land NaN", np.isnan(a[:, ~wet]).all()); ok("second field", b[:, wet] - g[:, wet], 0)
    S2 = np.array([[1., 2.], [3., 4.]]); Z = np.array([[1., 0.], [0., 2.]])
    ok("linear gram", Mo.gram(Z) - [[1, 0], [0, 4]], 0); ok("poly gram", Mo.gram(Z, "poly", 2, 1.) - [[4, 1], [1, 25]], 0); ok("poly default scale", Mo.gram(Z, "poly")[1, 1] - (1+4/2.5)**2, 1e-13)
    lam = np.array([1.0005, 0.9, 1.01, np.exp(.2j)]); ok("unit circle", Mo.mask_unit_circle(lam) * 1 - [1, 0, 0, 1], 0); ok("not growing", Mo.mask_not_growing(lam) * 1 - [1, 1, 0, 1], 0)
    ct = 1j*2*np.pi/np.array([10., 50., 200., -50.]); ok("period band", Mo.mask_period(ct, 20, 100)*1 - [0, 1, 0, 1], 0); ok("one per pair", Mo.mask_one_per_pair(np.array([1j, -1j, 0j]))*1 - [1, 0, 1], 0)
    mds = np.array([[1., 3.], [0., 4.]]); ok("top energy: |1|*1 < |1|*5", Mo.mask_top_energy(mds, np.ones(2), 1)*1 - [0, 1], 0)
    m2, a2 = Mo.apply_mask(np.array([False, True]), mds, np.array([9, 8])); ok("apply", m2[:, 0] - [3, 4], 0); ok("apply rest", a2 - [8], 0)
    lm = np.array([.9*np.exp(.3j)]); ok("exact", Mo.time_dynamics(lm, 4)[0] - lm**np.arange(4), 1e-14); ok("undamped", Mo.time_dynamics(lm, 4, "undamped")[0] - np.exp(.3j*np.arange(4)), 1e-14)
    ph = np.array([[1+1j], [2.]]); ok("reconstruct", Mo.reconstruct(ph, np.array([2.]), lm, 4) - (ph*2*lm**np.arange(4)).real, 1e-13)

py-kits › modredkit › modes › gram

gram

The snapshot kernel matrix for kernel DMD.

Description

A linear kernel gives plain DMD in kernel form; a polynomial one captures some nonlinear interactions between snapshots.

$$K = X^{T} X \ \text{(linear)},\qquad K = \big(1 + X^{T} X / c\big)^{d} \ \text{(poly)},\qquad c = \overline{\mathrm{diag}(X^{T} X)}$$

Syntax

S2 = gram(X)S2 = gram(X, kind='linear', degree=2, scale=None)

Input Arguments

X — float
(n, m) snapshots, one per column
kind — str — default 'linear'
'linear', X^T X, or 'poly', (1 + X^T X / scale)^degree
degree — int — default 2
Degree of the polynomial kernel
scale — float — default None
Scale of the polynomial kernel; the mean of the diagonal of X^T X by default

Output Arguments

S2 — float
(m, m) kernel matrix. Raises ValueError for another kind

Example

ok("linear gram", Mo.gram(Z) - [[1, 0], [0, 4]], 0); ok("poly gram", Mo.gram(Z, "poly", 2, 1.) - [[4, 1], [1, 25]], 0); ok("poly default scale", Mo.gram(Z, "poly")[1, 1] - (1+4/2.5)**2, 1e-13)

The modes that do not grow.

Description

$$|\lambda_k| \le 1 + \text{tol}$$

Syntax

mask = mask_not_growing(dt_eig)mask = mask_not_growing(dt_eig, tol=0.001)

Input Arguments

dt_eig — complex
Discrete-time eigenvalues
tol — float — default 0.001
Margin above 1

Output Arguments

mask — bool
True for the modes kept

Example

lam = np.array([1.0005, 0.9, 1.01, np.exp(.2j)]); ok("unit circle", Mo.mask_unit_circle(lam) * 1 - [1, 0, 0, 1], 0); ok("not growing", Mo.mask_not_growing(lam) * 1 - [1, 1, 0, 1], 0)
Whole test
with test("modredkit.modes.pack", "modredkit.modes.unpack", "modredkit.modes.gram", "modredkit.modes.mask_unit_circle", "modredkit.modes.mask_not_growing", "modredkit.modes.mask_period", "modredkit.modes.mask_one_per_pair", "modredkit.modes.mask_top_energy", "modredkit.modes.apply_mask", "modredkit.modes.time_dynamics", "modredkit.modes.reconstruct"):
    f = np.arange(24.).reshape(4, 2, 3); wet = np.array([[1, 1, 0], [0, 1, 1]], bool); g = 2*f; X = Mo.pack([f, g], [wet, wet]); yes("shape", X.shape == (8, 4))
    a, b = Mo.unpack(X, [wet, wet]); ok("field", a[:, wet] - f[:, wet], 0); yes("land NaN", np.isnan(a[:, ~wet]).all()); ok("second field", b[:, wet] - g[:, wet], 0)
    S2 = np.array([[1., 2.], [3., 4.]]); Z = np.array([[1., 0.], [0., 2.]])
    ok("linear gram", Mo.gram(Z) - [[1, 0], [0, 4]], 0); ok("poly gram", Mo.gram(Z, "poly", 2, 1.) - [[4, 1], [1, 25]], 0); ok("poly default scale", Mo.gram(Z, "poly")[1, 1] - (1+4/2.5)**2, 1e-13)
    lam = np.array([1.0005, 0.9, 1.01, np.exp(.2j)]); ok("unit circle", Mo.mask_unit_circle(lam) * 1 - [1, 0, 0, 1], 0); ok("not growing", Mo.mask_not_growing(lam) * 1 - [1, 1, 0, 1], 0)
    ct = 1j*2*np.pi/np.array([10., 50., 200., -50.]); ok("period band", Mo.mask_period(ct, 20, 100)*1 - [0, 1, 0, 1], 0); ok("one per pair", Mo.mask_one_per_pair(np.array([1j, -1j, 0j]))*1 - [1, 0, 1], 0)
    mds = np.array([[1., 3.], [0., 4.]]); ok("top energy: |1|*1 < |1|*5", Mo.mask_top_energy(mds, np.ones(2), 1)*1 - [0, 1], 0)
    m2, a2 = Mo.apply_mask(np.array([False, True]), mds, np.array([9, 8])); ok("apply", m2[:, 0] - [3, 4], 0); ok("apply rest", a2 - [8], 0)
    lm = np.array([.9*np.exp(.3j)]); ok("exact", Mo.time_dynamics(lm, 4)[0] - lm**np.arange(4), 1e-14); ok("undamped", Mo.time_dynamics(lm, 4, "undamped")[0] - np.exp(.3j*np.arange(4)), 1e-14)
    ph = np.array([[1+1j], [2.]]); ok("reconstruct", Mo.reconstruct(ph, np.array([2.]), lm, 4) - (ph*2*lm**np.arange(4)).real, 1e-13)

True for the modes kept

py-kits › modredkit › modes › time_dynamics

time_dynamics

The time behaviour of each mode over a number of snapshots.

Description

'undamped' keeps only the phase of each eigenvalue, so modes oscillate without growing or decaying, for example to extend a noise forcing beyond the record.

$$T_{k,t} = \lambda_k^{\,t}\ \text{(exact)},\qquad T_{k,t} = e^{i t \arg \lambda_k}\ \text{(undamped)}$$

Syntax

dyn = time_dynamics(dt_eig, nt)dyn = time_dynamics(dt_eig, nt, kind='exact')

Input Arguments

dt_eig — complex
(r,) discrete-time eigenvalues
nt — int
Number of snapshots
kind — str — default 'exact'
'exact', dt_eig^t, or 'undamped', keeping only the phase of dt_eig

Output Arguments

dyn — complex
(r, nt). Raises ValueError for another kind

Example

lm = np.array([.9*np.exp(.3j)]); ok("exact", Mo.time_dynamics(lm, 4)[0] - lm**np.arange(4), 1e-14); ok("undamped", Mo.time_dynamics(lm, 4, "undamped")[0] - np.exp(.3j*np.arange(4)), 1e-14)
Whole test
with test("modredkit.modes.pack", "modredkit.modes.unpack", "modredkit.modes.gram", "modredkit.modes.mask_unit_circle", "modredkit.modes.mask_not_growing", "modredkit.modes.mask_period", "modredkit.modes.mask_one_per_pair", "modredkit.modes.mask_top_energy", "modredkit.modes.apply_mask", "modredkit.modes.time_dynamics", "modredkit.modes.reconstruct"):
    f = np.arange(24.).reshape(4, 2, 3); wet = np.array([[1, 1, 0], [0, 1, 1]], bool); g = 2*f; X = Mo.pack([f, g], [wet, wet]); yes("shape", X.shape == (8, 4))
    a, b = Mo.unpack(X, [wet, wet]); ok("field", a[:, wet] - f[:, wet], 0); yes("land NaN", np.isnan(a[:, ~wet]).all()); ok("second field", b[:, wet] - g[:, wet], 0)
    S2 = np.array([[1., 2.], [3., 4.]]); Z = np.array([[1., 0.], [0., 2.]])
    ok("linear gram", Mo.gram(Z) - [[1, 0], [0, 4]], 0); ok("poly gram", Mo.gram(Z, "poly", 2, 1.) - [[4, 1], [1, 25]], 0); ok("poly default scale", Mo.gram(Z, "poly")[1, 1] - (1+4/2.5)**2, 1e-13)
    lam = np.array([1.0005, 0.9, 1.01, np.exp(.2j)]); ok("unit circle", Mo.mask_unit_circle(lam) * 1 - [1, 0, 0, 1], 0); ok("not growing", Mo.mask_not_growing(lam) * 1 - [1, 1, 0, 1], 0)
    ct = 1j*2*np.pi/np.array([10., 50., 200., -50.]); ok("period band", Mo.mask_period(ct, 20, 100)*1 - [0, 1, 0, 1], 0); ok("one per pair", Mo.mask_one_per_pair(np.array([1j, -1j, 0j]))*1 - [1, 0, 1], 0)
    mds = np.array([[1., 3.], [0., 4.]]); ok("top energy: |1|*1 < |1|*5", Mo.mask_top_energy(mds, np.ones(2), 1)*1 - [0, 1], 0)
    m2, a2 = Mo.apply_mask(np.array([False, True]), mds, np.array([9, 8])); ok("apply", m2[:, 0] - [3, 4], 0); ok("apply rest", a2 - [8], 0)
    lm = np.array([.9*np.exp(.3j)]); ok("exact", Mo.time_dynamics(lm, 4)[0] - lm**np.arange(4), 1e-14); ok("undamped", Mo.time_dynamics(lm, 4, "undamped")[0] - np.exp(.3j*np.arange(4)), 1e-14)
    ph = np.array([[1+1j], [2.]]); ok("reconstruct", Mo.reconstruct(ph, np.array([2.]), lm, 4) - (ph*2*lm**np.arange(4)).real, 1e-13)

py-kits › modredkit

pod

Snapshot POD, written for py-kits from the theory in the POD notes of the earlier model-reduction work. An older eigenproblem-based version existed in the earlier DMD code; neither is in this repository.

Snapshot matrices are (n, m): n spatial points, m snapshots, as in dmd.py. Build them with dmd.st_unravel.

Functions

rank_from_energyThe smallest rank whose modes hold a share of the total variance.
podProper orthogonal decomposition of a snapshot matrix.
reconstructRebuild the snapshot matrix from the output of pod.
pod_multiJoint POD of several fields that share time, such as u, v and w.
pod_multi.apply_wApply one field's weights to its anomalies.
py-kits › modredkit › pod › rank_from_energy

rank_from_energy

The smallest rank whose modes hold a share of the total variance.

Description

$$r = \min\Big\{ r : \frac{\sum_{k \le r} S_k^2}{\sum_k S_k^2} \ge \tau \Big\}$$

Syntax

r = rank_from_energy(S)r = rank_from_energy(S, energy=0.99)

Input Arguments

S — float
Singular values, in decreasing order
energy — float — default 0.99
Share of the variance, sum of S^2, to keep

Output Arguments

r — int
Rank, at most len(S)

Example

ok("rank, energy", P.rank_from_energy(np.array([2., 1.]), .79) - 1, 0); ok("rank, energy above first", P.rank_from_energy(np.array([2., 1.]), .81) - 2, 0)
Whole test
with test("modredkit.pod.pod", "modredkit.pod.reconstruct", "modredkit.pod.rank_from_energy", "modredkit.pod.pod_multi"):
    n, m = 80, 200; x = np.linspace(0, 2*np.pi, n, endpoint=False); ph1, ph2 = np.sin(x)*np.sqrt(2/n), np.cos(2*x)*np.sqrt(2/n)
    t = 2*np.pi*5*np.arange(m)/m; X = 7*ph1[:, None]*np.sin(t) + 3*ph2[:, None]*np.cos(t)
    U, S, C, mu = P.pod(X, r=2); ok("sigma_1, sigma_2", S - [7*np.sqrt(m/2), 3*np.sqrt(m/2)], 1e-11); ok("mode 1 up to sign", np.abs(U[:, 0]@ph1) - 1, 1e-12); ok("mode 2 up to sign", np.abs(U[:, 1]@ph2) - 1, 1e-12)
    ok("reconstruction", P.reconstruct(U, C, mu) - X, 1e-12); ok("mean removed", (X+5).shape[0] - n, 0)
    U5, S5, C5, mu5 = P.pod(X+5, r=2); ok("mean recovered", mu5 - 5, 1e-12)
    ok("rank, energy", P.rank_from_energy(np.array([2., 1.]), .79) - 1, 0); ok("rank, energy above first", P.rank_from_energy(np.array([2., 1.]), .81) - 2, 0)
    w = 1 + (np.arange(n) % 3); Uw, Sw, Cw, _ = P.pod(X, r=2, weights=w); ok("weighted orthonormality", Uw.T @ (w[:, None]*Uw) - np.eye(2), 1e-12)
    ok("weighted reconstruction", P.reconstruct(Uw, Cw) - (X - X.mean(1, keepdims=True)), 1e-11)
    Y = np.vstack([X, 2*X[::-1]+np.cos(3*x)[:, None]*np.sin(2*t)]); Um, Sm, Cm, _ = P.pod_multi([Y[:n], Y[n:]], r=3); U1, S1, C1, _ = P.pod(Y, r=3)
    ok("pod_multi singular values", Sm - S1, 1e-9); ok("pod_multi coeffs up to sign", np.abs(np.abs(Cm*C1).sum(1)/(S1**2)) - 1, 1e-9)

py-kits › modredkit › pod › pod

pod

Proper orthogonal decomposition of a snapshot matrix.

Description

POD finds the spatial patterns that capture the most variance, each with a time series: the basis of reduced models. With weights, such as cell volumes, the modes are orthonormal in that weighted inner product, so cells count by their size.

Weights must be strictly positive: remove land points first.

$$W^{1/2}(X - \bar X) = U S V^{T},\qquad \text{modes} = W^{-1/2} U_r,\qquad \text{coeffs} = S_r V_r^{T}$$

Syntax

modes, S, coeffs, mean = pod(X)modes, S, coeffs, mean = pod(X, r=None, weights=None, remove_mean=True)

Input Arguments

X — float
(n, m) snapshots, one per column
r — int — default None
Modes kept, None for all
weights — float — default None
(n,) strictly positive weights, or None; remove land points first
remove_mean — bool — default True
Subtract the time mean first

Output Arguments

modes — float
(n, r) spatial modes
S — float
(r,) singular values, of the weighted matrix
coeffs — float
(r, m) time coefficients, S times the right singular vectors
mean — float
(n,) time mean, zeros without remove_mean

Example

U, S, C, mu = P.pod(X, r=2); ok("sigma_1, sigma_2", S - [7*np.sqrt(m/2), 3*np.sqrt(m/2)], 1e-11); ok("mode 1 up to sign", np.abs(U[:, 0]@ph1) - 1, 1e-12); ok("mode 2 up to sign", np.abs(U[:, 1]@ph2) - 1, 1e-12)
U5, S5, C5, mu5 = P.pod(X+5, r=2); ok("mean recovered", mu5 - 5, 1e-12)
w = 1 + (np.arange(n) % 3); Uw, Sw, Cw, _ = P.pod(X, r=2, weights=w); ok("weighted orthonormality", Uw.T @ (w[:, None]*Uw) - np.eye(2), 1e-12)
Y = np.vstack([X, 2*X[::-1]+np.cos(3*x)[:, None]*np.sin(2*t)]); Um, Sm, Cm, _ = P.pod_multi([Y[:n], Y[n:]], r=3); U1, S1, C1, _ = P.pod(Y, r=3)

py-kits › modredkit › pod › pod_multi

pod_multi

Joint POD of several fields that share time, such as u, v and w.

Description

The modes of the fields are found together from one time correlation matrix summed over the fields, so each mode is a coherent pattern across all of them. This is the method of snapshots, cheap when there are fewer snapshots than points.

Modes with an eigenvalue below tol times the largest are dropped.

$$C = \sum_f A_f^{T} W_f A_f = V S^2 V^{T},\qquad \text{modes}_f = A_f V S^{-1},\qquad \text{coeffs} = S V^{T}$$

Syntax

modes, S, coeffs, means = pod_multi(fields)modes, S, coeffs, means = pod_multi(fields, r=None, weights=None, remove_mean=True, tol=1e-12)

Input Arguments

fields — list
(n_i, m) snapshot matrix of each field
r — int — default None
Modes kept, None for all
weights — list — default None
Per field: None, (n_i,) diagonal weights or an (n_i, n_i) matrix
remove_mean — bool — default True
Subtract each field's time mean
tol — float — default 1e-12
Modes with eigenvalue below tol times the largest are dropped

Output Arguments

modes — list
(n_i, r) spatial modes of each field, jointly orthonormal in the weighted product
S — float
(r,) singular values
coeffs — float
(r, m) time coefficients
means — list
(n_i,) time mean of each field

Example

Y = np.vstack([X, 2*X[::-1]+np.cos(3*x)[:, None]*np.sin(2*t)]); Um, Sm, Cm, _ = P.pod_multi([Y[:n], Y[n:]], r=3); U1, S1, C1, _ = P.pod(Y, r=3)
Whole test
with test("modredkit.pod.pod", "modredkit.pod.reconstruct", "modredkit.pod.rank_from_energy", "modredkit.pod.pod_multi"):
    n, m = 80, 200; x = np.linspace(0, 2*np.pi, n, endpoint=False); ph1, ph2 = np.sin(x)*np.sqrt(2/n), np.cos(2*x)*np.sqrt(2/n)
    t = 2*np.pi*5*np.arange(m)/m; X = 7*ph1[:, None]*np.sin(t) + 3*ph2[:, None]*np.cos(t)
    U, S, C, mu = P.pod(X, r=2); ok("sigma_1, sigma_2", S - [7*np.sqrt(m/2), 3*np.sqrt(m/2)], 1e-11); ok("mode 1 up to sign", np.abs(U[:, 0]@ph1) - 1, 1e-12); ok("mode 2 up to sign", np.abs(U[:, 1]@ph2) - 1, 1e-12)
    ok("reconstruction", P.reconstruct(U, C, mu) - X, 1e-12); ok("mean removed", (X+5).shape[0] - n, 0)
    U5, S5, C5, mu5 = P.pod(X+5, r=2); ok("mean recovered", mu5 - 5, 1e-12)
    ok("rank, energy", P.rank_from_energy(np.array([2., 1.]), .79) - 1, 0); ok("rank, energy above first", P.rank_from_energy(np.array([2., 1.]), .81) - 2, 0)
    w = 1 + (np.arange(n) % 3); Uw, Sw, Cw, _ = P.pod(X, r=2, weights=w); ok("weighted orthonormality", Uw.T @ (w[:, None]*Uw) - np.eye(2), 1e-12)
    ok("weighted reconstruction", P.reconstruct(Uw, Cw) - (X - X.mean(1, keepdims=True)), 1e-11)
    Y = np.vstack([X, 2*X[::-1]+np.cos(3*x)[:, None]*np.sin(2*t)]); Um, Sm, Cm, _ = P.pod_multi([Y[:n], Y[n:]], r=3); U1, S1, C1, _ = P.pod(Y, r=3)
    ok("pod_multi singular values", Sm - S1, 1e-9); ok("pod_multi coeffs up to sign", np.abs(np.abs(Cm*C1).sum(1)/(S1**2)) - 1, 1e-9)

py-kits

diagkit

Diagnostics of model output and of data: metrics, flow quantities, statistics, spectra and maps.

Once a model has run, or a reduced model has been built, it has to be judged against a reference. diagkit holds the measures used for that: error and pattern metrics and a relative entropy for ensembles, strain, vorticity and the Okubo-Weiss parameter, kinetic energy and anomalies, spectra in space and time, conservation checks, and the helpers for maps of the study regions.

Modules

metricsweighted rms, rms error, pattern correlation and Gaussian relative entropy
flowstrain, vorticity and the Okubo-Weiss parameter on a uniform C grid
statsanomalies, kinetic energy, horizontal means and the kinetic energy spectrum
spectraisotropic spectra in space and power spectra in time
conservationvolume means of tracers and layer volumes, to check conservation
fancy_plotscolormaps, the study regions and maps that locate them
py-kits › diagkit

conservation

Conservation-checking routines for NEMO tracer fields: volume-weighted averages over arbitrary depth ranges, and the 3D wet-point mask they need.

Promoted out of the earlier salinity conservation notebook (the volume-weighted salinity check developed while debugging a surface-salinity drop), so the same method can be reused for other tracers/runs without copy-pasting the notebook cells.

Functions

wet_mask_3dThe 3D wet-point mask from the number of wet levels of each column.
volume_weighted_meanVolume-weighted mean of a tracer over a range of levels, at every time.
py-kits › diagkit › conservation › wet_mask_3d

wet_mask_3d

The 3D wet-point mask from the number of wet levels of each column.

Description

Domain files store, for each column, how many levels are wet; volume integrals need the mask on every level. A level k, counted from 0, is wet when k + 1 <= bottom_level, so land columns, with 0, are dry everywhere.

$$m_{k,j,i} = 1 \text{ if } k + 1 \le \text{bottom\_level}_{j,i},\ 0 \text{ otherwise}$$

Syntax

mask3d = wet_mask_3d(bottom_level, jpk)

Input Arguments

bottom_level — int
(y, x) array from domain_cfg.nc
jpk — int
number of vertical levels

Output Arguments

mask3d — float
(k, y, x) wet-point mask, 1.0/0.0

Example

bl = np.array([[2, 1], [0, 2]]); m = cons.wet_mask_3d(bl, 3); ok("sum over k = bottom_level", m.sum(0) - bl, 0)
Whole test
with test("diagkit.conservation.wet_mask_3d", "diagkit.conservation.volume_weighted_mean"):
    bl = np.array([[2, 1], [0, 2]]); m = cons.wet_mask_3d(bl, 3); ok("sum over k = bottom_level", m.sum(0) - bl, 0)
    e3 = np.array([1., 3., 5.])[None, :, None, None]*np.ones((2, 3, 2, 2)); ar = np.array([[1., 2.], [9., 4.]])
    so = np.array([10., 20., 99.])[None, :, None, None]*np.ones((2, 3, 2, 2))
    ms, vol = cons.volume_weighted_mean(so, e3, m, ar)
    V1 = 1*(1+2+4); V2 = 3*(1+4)
    ok("mean", ms - (10*V1+20*V2)/(V1+V2), 1e-13); ok("volume", vol - (V1+V2), 1e-13)
    ms2, _ = cons.volume_weighted_mean(so, e3, m, ar, 1, 2); ok("one layer", ms2 - 20, 1e-13)

py-kits › diagkit › conservation › volume_weighted_mean

volume_weighted_mean

Volume-weighted mean of a tracer over a range of levels, at every time.

Description

A conserved tracer's volume mean should not drift in a closed basin; tracking it, and the layer volume beside it, checks conservation. The layer volume should stay nearly constant.

$$\bar s(t) = \frac{\sum_{k,j,i} s\, e_{3t}\, A\, m}{\sum_{k,j,i} e_{3t}\, A\, m},\qquad V(t) = \sum_{k,j,i} e_{3t}\, A\, m,\qquad k_{lo} \le k < k_{hi}$$

Syntax

mean_s, layer_volume = volume_weighted_mean(so, e3t, mask3d, area)mean_s, layer_volume = volume_weighted_mean(so, e3t, mask3d, area, k_lo=0, k_hi=None)

Input Arguments

so — float
(time, k, y, x) tracer field
e3t — float
(time, k, y, x) cell thickness
mask3d — float
(k, y, x) wet-point mask, from wet_mask_3d
area — float
(y, x) cell area (e.g. e1t*e2t)
k_lo — int — default 0
first level of the range (inclusive)
k_hi — int — default None
last level of the range (exclusive); defaults to all remaining levels

Output Arguments

mean_s — float
(time,) volume-weighted mean of `so`
layer_volume — float
(time,) total volume of the layer - a conservation sanity check, not just an intermediate: it should stay ~constant.

Example

ms, vol = cons.volume_weighted_mean(so, e3, m, ar)
ms2, _ = cons.volume_weighted_mean(so, e3, m, ar, 1, 2); ok("one layer", ms2 - 20, 1e-13)
Whole test
with test("diagkit.conservation.wet_mask_3d", "diagkit.conservation.volume_weighted_mean"):
    bl = np.array([[2, 1], [0, 2]]); m = cons.wet_mask_3d(bl, 3); ok("sum over k = bottom_level", m.sum(0) - bl, 0)
    e3 = np.array([1., 3., 5.])[None, :, None, None]*np.ones((2, 3, 2, 2)); ar = np.array([[1., 2.], [9., 4.]])
    so = np.array([10., 20., 99.])[None, :, None, None]*np.ones((2, 3, 2, 2))
    ms, vol = cons.volume_weighted_mean(so, e3, m, ar)
    V1 = 1*(1+2+4); V2 = 3*(1+4)
    ok("mean", ms - (10*V1+20*V2)/(V1+V2), 1e-13); ok("volume", vol - (V1+V2), 1e-13)
    ms2, _ = cons.volume_weighted_mean(so, e3, m, ar, 1, 2); ok("one layer", ms2 - 20, 1e-13)

fancy_plots

1. Project (INRIA) custom diverging colormaps -- same blue/white/red structure as matplotlib's RdBu/RdBu_r, but with project-specific endpoint colors instead of ColorBrewer's.

2. The AREAS OF INTEREST of the eORCA1 analysis, written in stone (ZONES, AGRIF_BOX, ZONE_COLOR, ZONE_BOX_EORCA1), and the region LOCATOR built on them (plot_zone_locator): a minimal Equal Earth land/ocean map with one area outlined, small enough to be dropped into a corner of any other figure. cartopy is imported lazily, inside the functions that need it, so importing this module for the colormaps alone does not need cartopy.

Functions

latlon_boxThe index box of the grid points inside a latitude-longitude rectangle.
zone_boxesThe index boxes of the four study zones and of the AGRIF nest.
seam_maskThe cells to hide so that pcolormesh does not stretch quads across the map.
zone_outline_lonlatPolylines outlining a zone, along its grid-index perimeter.
plot_zone_locatorA small map showing where a zone is: the land silhouette with the zone outlined.
py-kits › diagkit › fancy_plots › latlon_box

latlon_box

The index box of the grid points inside a latitude-longitude rectangle.

Description

On a curvilinear grid a region given in degrees is not an index range; this finds the smallest box of indices holding all the points inside it. The upper bounds are moved down so each side has an even length, which spectral routines need.

$$(j_0, j_1, i_0, i_1) = \text{bounding box of } \{(j,i) : \varphi_{1} < \varphi_{j,i} < \varphi_{2},\ \lambda_{1} < \lambda_{j,i} < \lambda_{2}\}$$

Syntax

box = latlon_box(nav_lat, nav_lon, lat_bnds, lon_bnds)

Input Arguments

nav_lat — float
(y, x) latitudes, in degrees
nav_lon — float
(y, x) longitudes, in degrees
lat_bnds — tuple
(south, north), exclusive
lon_bnds — tuple
(west, east), exclusive

Output Arguments

box — tuple
(j0, j1, i0, i1)

Example

box = fp.latlon_box(lat, lon, (0, 10), (20, 30)); ok("box", np.array(box) - [90, 100, 200, 210], 0)
Whole test
with test("diagkit.fancy_plots.latlon_box", "diagkit.fancy_plots.zone_boxes", "diagkit.fancy_plots.seam_mask", "diagkit.fancy_plots.zone_outline_lonlat", "diagkit.fancy_plots.plot_zone_locator"):
    lat = np.arange(-89.5, 90)[:, None]*np.ones((180, 360)); lon = np.arange(-179.5, 180)[None]*np.ones((180, 360))
    box = fp.latlon_box(lat, lon, (0, 10), (20, 30)); ok("box", np.array(box) - [90, 100, 200, 210], 0)
    z = fp.zone_boxes(lat, lon); yes("5 zones", len(z) == 5)
    lon2 = lon.copy(); yes("no seam on a smooth grid inside", not fp.seam_mask(lon2[20:-20, 20:-20], lat[20:-20, 20:-20], 0).any())
    lon3 = (lon + 100 + 180) % 360 - 180; yes("seam found at the jump", fp.seam_mask(lon3, lat, 0).any())
    o = fp.zone_outline_lonlat("GulfStream", lon, lat, z); yes("four sides", len(o) == 4); ok("south side latitude", o[0][1] - lat[z["GulfStream"][0], 0], 0)
    yes("ACC is two circles", len(fp.zone_outline_lonlat("ACC", lon, lat, z)) == 2)
    ax = fp.plot_zone_locator("Nino3", lon, lat, np.zeros_like(lat, bool), z); yes("locator returns axes", ax is not None); plt.close("all")

py-kits › diagkit › fancy_plots › seam_mask

seam_mask

The cells to hide so that pcolormesh does not stretch quads across the map.

Description

On eORCA1 the longitude wraps along a cut that runs diagonally through index space, and the north fold adds another. Plotted naively, cells across the cut become long bands over the whole map. Each point is projected, and cells whose jump to an index neighbour is far above the median spacing are masked, so it works for any central longitude.

$$\text{mask}_{j,i} = \|\mathbf{p}_{j,i} - \mathbf{p}_{\text{nb}}\| > \text{factor} \cdot \mathrm{median}\|\Delta \mathbf{p}\| \text{ for any index neighbour}$$

Syntax

mask = seam_mask(nav_lon, nav_lat, central_longitude)mask = seam_mask(nav_lon, nav_lat, central_longitude, factor=8)

Input Arguments

nav_lon — float
(y, x) longitudes, in degrees
nav_lat — float
(y, x) latitudes, in degrees
central_longitude — float
Of ccrs.EqualEarth
factor — float — default 8
Jumps above factor times the median spacing count as a cut

Output Arguments

mask — bool
(y, x) True on cells touching a cut

Example

lon2 = lon.copy(); yes("no seam on a smooth grid inside", not fp.seam_mask(lon2[20:-20, 20:-20], lat[20:-20, 20:-20], 0).any())
lon3 = (lon + 100 + 180) % 360 - 180; yes("seam found at the jump", fp.seam_mask(lon3, lat, 0).any())
Whole test

zone_outline_lonlat

Polylines outlining a zone, along its grid-index perimeter.

Description

On a curvilinear grid the index perimeter of a zone and an ideal latitude-longitude rectangle differ visibly; the outline drawn is the region actually studied. The Antarctic Circumpolar Current zone is drawn as two circles at its latitude bounds, since its rows cross the index-space seam.

$$\big(\lambda, \varphi\big) \text{ along rows } j_0, j_1 - 1 \text{ and columns } i_0, i_1 - 1$$

Key of zone_box
nav_lon — float
(y, x) longitudes, in degrees
nav_lat — float
(y, x) latitudes, in degrees
zone_box — dict
From zone_boxes

Output Arguments

lines — list
(lons, lats) arrays, one per side

Whole test
with test("diagkit.fancy_plots.latlon_box", "diagkit.fancy_plots.zone_boxes", "diagkit.fancy_plots.seam_mask", "diagkit.fancy_plots.zone_outline_lonlat", "diagkit.fancy_plots.plot_zone_locator"):
    lat = np.arange(-89.5, 90)[:, None]*np.ones((180, 360)); lon = np.arange(-179.5, 180)[None]*np.ones((180, 360))
    box = fp.latlon_box(lat, lon, (0, 10), (20, 30)); ok("box", np.array(box) - [90, 100, 200, 210], 0)
    z = fp.zone_boxes(lat, lon); yes("5 zones", len(z) == 5)
    lon2 = lon.copy(); yes("no seam on a smooth grid inside", not fp.seam_mask(lon2[20:-20, 20:-20], lat[20:-20, 20:-20], 0).any())
    lon3 = (lon + 100 + 180) % 360 - 180; yes("seam found at the jump", fp.seam_mask(lon3, lat, 0).any())
    o = fp.zone_outline_lonlat("GulfStream", lon, lat, z); yes("four sides", len(o) == 4); ok("south side latitude", o[0][1] - lat[z["GulfStream"][0], 0], 0)
    yes("ACC is two circles", len(fp.zone_outline_lonlat("ACC", lon, lat, z)) == 2)
    ax = fp.plot_zone_locator("Nino3", lon, lat, np.zeros_like(lat, bool), z); yes("locator returns axes", ax is not None); plt.close("all")

py-kits › diagkit

flow

Strain, vorticity and Okubo-Weiss on a C-grid with uniform spacing (dx, dy scalars) and no boundary conditions; edge rows and columns stay zero. On ORCA grids this is only a local approximation: use a box away from the north fold. Ported from grad_py of the earlier analysis code.

Functions

_t_from_fAverage an F-point field onto interior T-points.
strain_normalNormal strain on interior T-points, on a uniform grid.
strain_shearShear strain on F-points, on a uniform grid.
vorticityRelative vorticity on F-points, on a uniform grid.
okubo_weissThe Okubo-Weiss parameter on T-points.
py-kits › diagkit › flow › _t_from_f

_t_from_f

Average an F-point field onto interior T-points.

Description

$$T_{j,i} = \tfrac14\big(F_{j-1,i-1} + F_{j,i-1} + F_{j,i} + F_{j-1,i}\big)$$

Syntax

T = _t_from_f(F)

Input Arguments

F — float
(..., ny, nx) F-point field

Output Arguments

T — float
(..., ny, nx) mean of the four F-points around each interior T-point, 0 on the outer rows and columns

Example

ok("_t_from_f of a constant", flow._t_from_f(np.ones((5, 5)))[1:-1, 1:-1] - 1, 0)
Whole test
with test("diagkit.flow.strain_normal", "diagkit.flow.strain_shear", "diagkit.flow.vorticity", "diagkit.flow.okubo_weiss", "diagkit.flow._t_from_f"):
    ny, nx = 20, 30; dx, dy = 2., 3.; jj, ii = np.mgrid[:ny, :nx].astype(float); xu, yu = (ii+.5)*dx, jj*dy; xv, yv = ii*dx, (jj+.5)*dy
    a, b, c, d = .3, -.7, 1.1, .2; u = a*xu + b*yu; v = c*xv + d*yv; I = (slice(2, -2), slice(2, -2))
    ok("s_n", flow.strain_normal(u, v, dx, dy)[I] - (a-d), 1e-12); ok("s_s", flow.strain_shear(u, v, dx, dy)[I] - (c+b), 1e-12)
    ok("vorticity", flow.vorticity(u, v, dx, dy)[I] - (c-b), 1e-12)
    ok("Okubo-Weiss", flow.okubo_weiss(u, v, dx, dy)[I] - ((a-d)**2+(c+b)**2-(c-b)**2), 1e-11)
    ok("_t_from_f of a constant", flow._t_from_f(np.ones((5, 5)))[1:-1, 1:-1] - 1, 0)
    Om = .5; ok("rotation W = -4 Omega^2", flow.okubo_weiss(-Om*yu, Om*xv, dx, dy)[I] + 4*Om*Om, 1e-12)

py-kits › diagkit › flow › strain_normal

strain_normal

Normal strain on interior T-points, on a uniform grid.

Description

The normal strain measures stretching along x against y. With the shear strain and the vorticity it separates straining flow from rotating flow.

$$s_n = \frac{u_{j,i} - u_{j,i-1}}{\Delta x} - \frac{v_{j,i} - v_{j-1,i}}{\Delta y}$$

Syntax

sn = strain_normal(u, v, dx, dy)

Input Arguments

u — float
(..., ny, nx) U-point velocity
v — float
(..., ny, nx) V-point velocity
dx — float
Grid spacing in x
dy — float
Grid spacing in y

Output Arguments

sn — float
(..., ny, nx), 0 on the outer rows and columns

py-kits › diagkit › flow › okubo_weiss

okubo_weiss

The Okubo-Weiss parameter on T-points.

Description

It separates eddies from the straining flow around them: negative where rotation dominates, inside eddy cores, and positive where strain dominates.

$$W = s_n^2 + s_s^2 - \zeta^2$$

Syntax

W = okubo_weiss(u, v, dx, dy)

Input Arguments

u — float
(..., ny, nx) U-point velocity
v — float
(..., ny, nx) V-point velocity
dx — float
Grid spacing in x
dy — float
Grid spacing in y

Output Arguments

W — float
(..., ny, nx) on T-points

Example

ok("Okubo-Weiss", flow.okubo_weiss(u, v, dx, dy)[I] - ((a-d)**2+(c+b)**2-(c-b)**2), 1e-11)
Om = .5; ok("rotation W = -4 Omega^2", flow.okubo_weiss(-Om*yu, Om*xv, dx, dy)[I] + 4*Om*Om, 1e-12)

py-kits › diagkit

metrics

Weighted comparison metrics. Spatial axes are the trailing weights.ndim axes. Ported from DiagnosticMetrics of the earlier analysis code.

Functions

_wmeanWeighted mean over the trailing axes covered by the weights.
rmsWeighted root mean square.
rmseWeighted root mean square error of an estimate against a reference.
pattern_correlationWeighted, uncentred pattern correlation, 1 for identical patterns.
gaussian_relative_entropyRelative entropy of a Gaussian estimate against a Gaussian reference, point by point.
averaged_greWeighted mean of the Gaussian relative entropy.
py-kits › diagkit › metrics › _wmean

_wmean

Weighted mean over the trailing axes covered by the weights.

Description

$$\langle q \rangle_w = \frac{\sum q\, w}{\sum w}$$

Syntax

mean = _wmean(q, weights)

Input Arguments

q — float
Field, whose last axes match weights
weights — float
Weights

Output Arguments

mean — float
Weighted mean, with the leading axes of q

Example

w = np.array([[1., 3.]]); ok("_wmean", metrics._wmean(np.array([[1., 5.]]), w) - 4, 0)
Whole test
with test("diagkit.metrics._wmean", "diagkit.metrics.rms", "diagkit.metrics.rmse", "diagkit.metrics.pattern_correlation", "diagkit.metrics.gaussian_relative_entropy", "diagkit.metrics.averaged_gre"):
    w = np.array([[1., 3.]]); ok("_wmean", metrics._wmean(np.array([[1., 5.]]), w) - 4, 0)
    ok("rms of a constant", metrics.rms(-2*np.ones((3, 4)), np.ones((3, 4))) - 2, 1e-14)
    f = np.sin(np.linspace(0, 2*np.pi, 64, endpoint=False))[None]; W = np.ones_like(f)
    ok("rmse", metrics.rmse(f+3, f, W) - 3, 1e-14)
    ok("corr(f, -2f) = -1", metrics.pattern_correlation(-2*f, f, W) + 1, 1e-14)
    ok("corr(sin, cos) = 0", metrics.pattern_correlation(f, np.cos(np.linspace(0, 2*np.pi, 64, endpoint=False))[None], W), 1e-14)
    ok("GRE identical", metrics.gaussian_relative_entropy(1., 1., 2., 2.), 1e-15)
    ok("GRE hand value", metrics.gaussian_relative_entropy(1., 0., 2., 1.) - .5*(.5 + .5 - 1 - np.log(.5)), 1e-14)
    ok("averaged GRE uniform", metrics.averaged_gre(W, 0*W, 2*W, W, W) - .5*(.5 + .5 - 1 - np.log(.5)), 1e-14)

py-kits › diagkit › metrics › rmse

rmse

Weighted root mean square error of an estimate against a reference.

Description

The usual measure of how far a model or a reduced model is from the reference, in the field's units.

$$\sqrt{\langle (e - o)^2 \rangle_w}$$

Syntax

rmse = rmse(estimator, observable, weights)

Input Arguments

py-kits › diagkit › metrics › gaussian_relative_entropy

gaussian_relative_entropy

Relative entropy of a Gaussian estimate against a Gaussian reference, point by point.

Description

It measures how much information is lost when the estimate replaces the reference, penalising both a wrong mean and a wrong spread, which suits comparing ensembles with their target.

$$\mathcal{R} = \tfrac12\Big[\frac{(\mu_e - \mu_o)^2}{\sigma_e^2} + \frac{\sigma_o^2}{\sigma_e^2} - 1 - \log\frac{\sigma_o^2}{\sigma_e^2}\Big]$$

Syntax

gre = gaussian_relative_entropy(est_avg, obs_avg, est_vnc, obs_vnc)

Input Arguments

est_avg — float
Mean of the estimate
obs_avg — float
Mean of the reference
est_vnc — float
Variance of the estimate
obs_vnc — float
Variance of the reference

Output Arguments

gre — float
0.5 [(est_avg - obs_avg)^2 / est_vnc + r - 1 - log r], r = obs_vnc / est_vnc

Example

ok("GRE identical", metrics.gaussian_relative_entropy(1., 1., 2., 2.), 1e-15)
ok("GRE hand value", metrics.gaussian_relative_entropy(1., 0., 2., 1.) - .5*(.5 + .5 - 1 - np.log(.5)), 1e-14)

py-kits › diagkit

spectra

Spatial and temporal power spectral density (PSD) tools.

Spatial: isotropic spectrum of a 2D/3D field, following the procedure in Durran et al. (2017), "Practical considerations for computing dimensional spectra from gridded data", http://doi.org/10.1175/MWR-D-17-0056.1

Temporal: periodogram-based PSD along the leading (time) axis of a field, optionally reduced over the trailing spatial axes by a weight array.

Author: Long Li, long.li@inria.fr

Francesco Tucciarone, francesco.tucciarone@inria.fr

Functions

init_2DwvnbThe wavenumbers of a 2D discrete Fourier transform, and of its isotropic spectrum.
init_3DwvnbThe wavenumbers of a 3D discrete Fourier transform, and of its isotropic spectrum.
iso_specThe isotropic spectrum, summing Fourier coefficients over rings of wavenumber.
temporal_psdPower spectral density in time, by periodogram, optionally summed over space with weights.
py-kits › diagkit › spectra › init_2Dwvnb

init_2Dwvnb

The wavenumbers of a 2D discrete Fourier transform, and of its isotropic spectrum.

Description

An isotropic spectrum sums the energy of all Fourier coefficients with the same wavenumber modulus. This gives that modulus for every coefficient, the rings to sum over and the scaling of the result.

$$k_x = \frac{2\pi}{n_x \Delta x}\,\{0, \dots, \tfrac{n_x}{2}-1, -\tfrac{n_x}{2}, \dots, -1\},\qquad |k| = \sqrt{k_x^2 + k_y^2},\qquad k_r = \Delta k_r\,\{1, \dots, \tfrac{\min(n_x, n_y)}{2}\}$$

Syntax

wv, kr, efac = init_2Dwvnb(nx, ny, dx, dy)

Input Arguments

nx — int
Points in x, even
ny — int
Points in y, even
dx — float
Spacing in x
dy — float
Spacing in y

Output Arguments

wv — float
(nx*ny,) wavenumber modulus of each Fourier coefficient, in the order of a flattened (ny, nx) array
kr — float
Isotropic wavenumbers, up to min(nx, ny)/2 steps of max(dkx, dky)
efac — float
Scaling of the spectrum for the DFT and the integration

Example

wv, kr, efc = spectra.init_2Dwvnb(n, n, dx, dx); ok("first ring at 2 pi / L", kr[0] - 1, 1e-12); ok("wavenumber count", wv.size - n*n, 0)
Whole test
with test("diagkit.spectra.init_2Dwvnb", "diagkit.spectra.iso_spec"):
    n = 64; L = 2*np.pi; dx = L/n; x = np.arange(n)*dx; f = np.cos(5*x)[None]*np.ones((n, n))
    wv, kr, efc = spectra.init_2Dwvnb(n, n, dx, dx); ok("first ring at 2 pi / L", kr[0] - 1, 1e-12); ok("wavenumber count", wv.size - n*n, 0)
    fh = np.abs(np.fft.fft2(f))**2; E = spectra.iso_spec(fh, wv, kr, efc)
    ok("Parseval", E.sum()*(kr[1]-kr[0]) - (f**2).mean(), 1e-12); ok("energy in the k=5 ring only", np.delete(E, 4), 1e-20)
    r = np.random.default_rng(0).standard_normal((n, n)); r -= r.mean(); F = np.fft.fft2(r); F[np.abs(wv.reshape(n, n)) > kr[-1]] = 0; r2 = np.fft.ifft2(F).real
    ok("Parseval, random field", rerr(spectra.iso_spec(np.abs(np.fft.fft2(r2))**2, wv, kr, efc).sum(), (r2**2).mean()), 1e-10)

py-kits › diagkit › spectra › iso_spec

iso_spec

The isotropic spectrum, summing Fourier coefficients over rings of wavenumber.

Description

The trailing two or three axes are spatial, three when their size matches the wavenumbers.

$$E(k_r) = c\sum_{|\,|k| - k_r| \le \Delta k_r / 2} \hat f(k)$$

Syntax

psdr = iso_spec(fh, wv, kr, efc)

Input Arguments

fh — float
(..., ny, nx) or (..., nz, ny, nx) spectral density, e.g. |FFT|^2
wv — float
From init_2Dwvnb or init_3Dwvnb
kr — float
Isotropic wavenumbers, same source
efc — float
Scaling factor, same source

Output Arguments

psdr — float
(..., len(kr)) isotropic spectrum

Example

fh = np.abs(np.fft.fft2(f))**2; E = spectra.iso_spec(fh, wv, kr, efc)
ok("Parseval, random field", rerr(spectra.iso_spec(np.abs(np.fft.fft2(r2))**2, wv, kr, efc).sum(), (r2**2).mean()), 1e-10)

    fh = np.abs(np.fft.fft2(f))**2; E = spectra.iso_spec(fh, wv, kr, efc)

py-kits › diagkit › spectra › temporal_psd

temporal_psd

Power spectral density in time, by periodogram, optionally summed over space with weights.

Description

The spectrum in time shows at which periods a field varies; summed over a region with weights it gives one spectrum for the whole region.

$$P(f) = \text{periodogram}(q)(f),\qquad \text{or}\ \sum_{j,i} w_{j,i}\, P_{j,i}(f)$$

Syntax

freq, psd = temporal_psd(q, fs)freq, psd = temporal_psd(q, fs, weights=None)

Input Arguments

q — float
Field, time along axis 0
fs — float
Sampling frequency [1/s]
weights — float — default None
Optional 2D weight array broadcast against q's trailing two axes; if given, the result is summed over those axes.

Output Arguments

freq — float
Frequency axis, shape (q.shape[0]//2 + 1,)
psd — float
PSD; same shape as q with axis 0 replaced by freq if weights is None, else weights applied and the trailing two axes summed away.

Example

fr, p = spectra.temporal_psd(q, fs); ok("integral = A^2/2", (p[:, 0, 0].sum()*(fr[1]-fr[0])) - 4.5, 1e-10); ok("peak", fr[np.argmax(p[:, 0, 0])] - f0, 1e-12)
fr, pw = spectra.temporal_psd(q, fs, np.ones((4, 4))/16); ok("weighted equals one point", pw - p[:, 0, 0], 1e-11)
Whole test
with test("diagkit.spectra.temporal_psd"):
    nt = 400; fs = 4.; f0 = 0.5; t = np.arange(nt)/fs; q = (3*np.sin(2*np.pi*f0*t))[:, None, None]*np.ones((nt, 4, 4))
    fr, p = spectra.temporal_psd(q, fs); ok("integral = A^2/2", (p[:, 0, 0].sum()*(fr[1]-fr[0])) - 4.5, 1e-10); ok("peak", fr[np.argmax(p[:, 0, 0])] - f0, 1e-12)
    fr, pw = spectra.temporal_psd(q, fs, np.ones((4, 4))/16); ok("weighted equals one point", pw - p[:, 0, 0], 1e-11)

stats

Functions

fluctuationsAnomalies in time, removing the means of the spin-up and of the rest separately.

py-kits › diagkit › stats › fluctuations

fluctuations

Anomalies in time, removing the means of the spin-up and of the rest separately.

Description

A model's first months drift towards equilibrium; removing one mean over the whole run would mix that drift into the anomalies.

$$q' = q - \overline{q}^{[0, d)} \text{ on } t < d,\qquad q' = q - \overline{q}^{[d, n)} \text{ on } t \ge d$$

Syntax

q_prime = fluctuations(q)q_prime = fluctuations(q, delay=0)

Input Arguments

q — float
(nt, ...) record
delay — int — default 0
Snapshots of spin-up, 0 for none

Output Arguments

q_prime — float
(nt, ...) anomalies

Example

q = np.arange(10.)[:, None, None]*np.ones((10, 3, 3)); fl = stats.fluctuations(q, 4)
Whole test
with test("diagkit.stats.fluctuations", "diagkit.stats.kinetic_energy", "diagkit.stats.hovmoller", "diagkit.stats.ke_spectrum"):
    q = np.arange(10.)[:, None, None]*np.ones((10, 3, 3)); fl = stats.fluctuations(q, 4)
    ok("spin-up anomalies", fl[:4].mean(0), 1e-14); ok("rest", fl[4:].mean(0), 1e-14); ok("value", fl[0, 0, 0] + 1.5, 1e-14)
    ok("KE interior", stats.kinetic_energy(3*np.ones((5, 5)), 4*np.ones((5, 5)))[1:-1, 1:-1] - 12.5, 1e-13)
    ok("Hovmoller", stats.hovmoller(q)[3] - 3, 0)

kinetic_energy

Kinetic energy on interior T-points, from velocities on the C grid.

Description

$$K = \tfrac14\big(u_{j,i-1}^2 + u_{j,i}^2 + v_{j-1,i}^2 + v_{j,i}^2\big) = \tfrac12\big(\overline{u^2} + \overline{v^2}\big)$$

v — float
(..., ny, nx) V-point velocity

Output Arguments

(..., ny, nx), 0 on the outer rows and columns

Horizontal mean, leaving time and any other leading axes.

py-kits › diagkit › stats › ke_spectrum

ke_spectrum

Isotropic kinetic energy spectrum on a uniform grid.

Description

How kinetic energy spreads across scales: its slope separates regimes of turbulence, and its fall-off shows the effective resolution of a model.

$$E(k_r) = \text{iso\_spec}\Big(\tfrac12\big(|\hat u|^2 + |\hat v|^2\big)\Big)$$

Syntax

kr, spec = ke_spectrum(u, v, dx, dy)

Input Arguments

u — float
(..., ny, nx) velocity; nx and ny even
v — float
(..., ny, nx) velocity
dx — float
Spacing in x
dy — float
Spacing in y

Output Arguments

kr — float
Isotropic wavenumbers
spec — float
(..., len(kr)) spectrum

Example

n = 64; dx = 2*np.pi/n; u = np.cos(5*np.arange(n)*dx)[None]*np.ones((n, n)); k, s = stats.ke_spectrum(u, 0*u, dx, dx)
Whole test

    ok("spin-up anomalies", fl[:4].mean(0), 1e-14); ok("rest", fl[4:].mean(0), 1e-14); ok("value", fl[0, 0, 0] + 1.5, 1e-14)
    ok("KE interior", stats.kinetic_energy(3*np.ones((5, 5)), 4*np.ones((5, 5)))[1:-1, 1:-1] - 12.5, 1e-13)

py-kits

gyrekit

What is specific to the GYRE configurations (R3, R9, R27): runs, masks and coarse-graining.

GYRE is NEMO's idealised double-gyre basin, used to test methods at several resolutions before the global ocean. gyrekit holds only what depends on it: where the runs are and how to read them, its masks and the passage between resolutions, and a standard summary of a run. Everything generic comes from the other kits.

Modules

runsthe experiments of each resolution and their files, from config/paths_<R>.yaml
gridsthe jet mask, matching grids between resolutions and coarse-graining of pressure fields
diagthe standard velocity diagnostics of a run
py-kits › gyrekit

diag

The velocity part of the old R3/R9 diagnostic, as one function over the other kits. Replaces the DIAG_NEMO class, which computed and wrote everything on creation.

Functions

velocity_summaryStandard diagnostics of GYRE velocities.
py-kits › gyrekit › diag › velocity_summary

velocity_summary

Standard diagnostics of GYRE velocities.

Description

One call gives what a GYRE run is usually judged by: mean flow, mean and eddy kinetic energy, their evolution, and their spectra in space and time. The spin-up is left out of means and spectra, and the points near the boundaries out of the time spectrum.

$$\text{MKE} = K(\bar u, \bar v),\qquad \text{EKE} = \overline{K(u', v')},\qquad \text{spectra of } K \text{ and } \tfrac12(P_u + P_v)$$

Syntax

summary = velocity_summary(u, v, dx, dy, dt)summary = velocity_summary(u, v, dx, dy, dt, delay=0, nb=13)

Input Arguments

u — float
(time, z, y, x) or (time, y, x) velocity
v — float
Same shape
dx — float
Spacing in x
dy — float
Spacing in y
dt — float
Time between snapshots
delay — int — default 0
Snapshots of spin-up left out of means and spectra
nb — int — default 13
Points near the boundaries left out of the time spectrum

Output Arguments

summary — dict
umean, vmean, mke, eke, hov_ke, hov_eke, k, spec_ke, freq, psd_eke

Example

r = Gd.velocity_summary(u, v, 1., 1., 1., delay=0, nb=2); I = (slice(2, -2), slice(2, -2))
Whole test
with test("gyrekit.diag.velocity_summary"):
    nt, ny, nx = 240, 32, 32; f0 = 1/24; t = np.arange(nt); U0, a = 2., 1.; u = (U0 + a*np.cos(2*np.pi*f0*t))[:, None, None]*np.ones((nt, ny, nx)); v = 0*u
    r = Gd.velocity_summary(u, v, 1., 1., 1., delay=0, nb=2); I = (slice(2, -2), slice(2, -2))
    ok("MKE", r["mke"][I] - .5*U0*U0, 1e-12); ok("EKE", r["eke"][I] - .25*a*a, 1e-12); ok("PSD peak", r["freq"][np.argmax(r["psd_eke"])] - f0, 1e-12)
    ok("PSD integrates to EKE", r["psd_eke"].sum()*(r["freq"][1]-r["freq"][0]) - .25*a*a, 1e-10); ok("no ring energy for a uniform flow", r["spec_ke"], 1e-20)

grids

GYRE masks and high-to-low resolution helpers. Ported from the mask and filter modules of the earlier GYRE analysis code. coarse_grain_T was not ported: it needs scipy's removed interp2d.

Functions

jet_maskA mask of the box around the GYRE jet.

py-kits › gyrekit › grids › jet_mask

jet_mask

A mask of the box around the GYRE jet.

Description

1 inside a latitude-longitude box around the jet, 0 outside it and within 150 grid units of the north and west edges, where boundary currents would dominate.

$$m = 1 \text{ if } |\varphi - \varphi_c| < w_\varphi,\ |\lambda - \lambda_c| < w_\lambda, \text{ away from the north and west edges}$$

Syntax

mask = jet_mask(lat, lon, dx, dy)mask = jet_mask(lat, lon, dx, dy, latc=29, lonc=-85, latw=5, lonw=20)

Input Arguments

lat — float
(y, x) latitudes, in degrees
lon — float
(y, x) longitudes, in degrees
dx — float
Spacing in x
dy — float
Spacing in y
latc — float — default 29
Centre latitude of the box
lonc — float — default -85
Centre longitude of the box
latw — float — default 5
Half-width of the box in latitude
lonw — float — default 20
Half-width of the box in longitude

Output Arguments

mask — int
(y, x) mask

Example

lat = np.arange(10., 50)[:, None]*np.ones((40, 60)); lon = np.arange(-115., -55)[None]*np.ones((40, 60)); jm = Gg.jet_mask(lat, lon, 10., 10.)
Whole test
with test("gyrekit.grids.area_int", "gyrekit.grids.coarse_grain_P", "gyrekit.grids.jet_mask", "gyrekit.grids.find_overlap"):
    ok("trapezoid of 1", Gg.area_int(np.ones((11, 21)), .5, .5) - 200, 1e-12)
    jj, ii = np.mgrid[:11, :21].astype(float); ok("trapezoid of x", Gg.area_int(ii, .5, .5) - 2000, 1e-11)
    rat = 3; ph = 2*np.ones((3*20+1, 3*30+1)); pl = Gg.coarse_grain_P(ph, rat); ok("area integral kept, relative", Gg.area_int(pl, .5, .5)/(Gg.area_int(ph, .5, .5)/rat**2) - 1, 1e-10)
    lat = np.arange(10., 50)[:, None]*np.ones((40, 60)); lon = np.arange(-115., -55)[None]*np.ones((40, 60)); jm = Gg.jet_mask(lat, lon, 10., 10.)
    ok("edges zero", [jm[-15:].max(), jm[:, :15].max()], 0); yes("inside the box", jm[int(29-10), int(-85+115)] == 1); yes("outside", jm[0, 30] == 0)
    hl = np.arange(38.)[:, None]*np.ones((38, 58)); hn = np.arange(58.)[None]*np.ones((38, 58)); ll = np.arange(20.)[:, None]*np.ones((20, 30)); ln = np.arange(30.)[None]*np.ones((20, 30)); c, r = Gg.find_overlap(hl, hn, ll, ln); yes("find_overlap ran (no analytic contract)", c.ndim == 1 and r.ndim == 1)

Area integral of a 2D array in grid units, with weights for the boundary rows and columns.

Weight of the west and east columns

py-kits › gyrekit › grids › coarse_grain_P

coarse_grain_P

Coarse-grain a high-resolution pressure-grid field, keeping its area integral.

Description

The field is smoothed with a Gaussian of sigma ratio/4 and subsampled every ratio points; a constant boundary value then restores the area integral of the original.

$$p_c = (G_{r/4} * p_h)_{\,r-1::r},\qquad p_{bc} = \frac{\int p_h / r^2 - \int p_c}{\text{boundary points} + 1}$$

Syntax

pl = coarse_grain_P(ph, ratio)

Input Arguments

ph — float
(y, x) high-resolution field
ratio — int
Resolution ratio

Output Arguments

pl — float
Coarse field, with one boundary row and column on each side

Example

rat = 3; ph = 2*np.ones((3*20+1, 3*30+1)); pl = Gg.coarse_grain_P(ph, rat); ok("area integral kept, relative", Gg.area_int(pl, .5, .5)/(Gg.area_int(ph, .5, .5)/rat**2) - 1, 1e-10)
Whole test

    hl = np.arange(38.)[:, None]*np.ones((38, 58)); hn = np.arange(58.)[None]*np.ones((38, 58)); ll = np.arange(20.)[:, None]*np.ones((20, 30)); ln = np.arange(30.)[None]*np.ones((20, 30)); c, r = Gg.find_overlap(hl, hn, ll, ln); yes("find_overlap ran (no analytic contract)", c.ndim == 1 and r.ndim == 1)

py-kits › gyrekit

runs

Find and read GYRE experiments from config/paths_R3.yaml and paths_R9.yaml. Replaces OpenYAML.yaml2dict of the earlier analysis code. The configs point to the result folders set in paths.toml (gyre_root).

Functions

experimentsThe GYRE experiments of a resolution, with their files.
gridfileThe path of the domain_cfg file of a GYRE resolution.
read_fieldRead a variable from several files, joined along time.
read_spacingThe uniform grid spacing of a GYRE domain_cfg file.
py-kits › gyrekit › runs › experiments

experiments

The GYRE experiments of a resolution, with their files.

Description

Paths come from paths_<resolution>.yaml, with the high-resolution runs included; they are not checked.

$$\{\text{name}: (\text{label}, \text{color}, \{\text{kind}: [\text{paths}]\})\}$$

Syntax

exps = experiments(resolution)

Input Arguments

resolution — str
'R3' or 'R9'

Output Arguments

exps — dict
{name: {'label', 'color', 'files': {kind: [paths]}}}

Example

ex = Gr.experiments("R3"); yes("experiments found", len(ex) > 0); e0 = next(iter(ex.values())); yes("all file kinds", set(e0["files"]) == set(Gr.KINDS)); yes("no double slash", "//" not in e0["files"]["uvelfile"][0])
Whole test
with test("gyrekit.runs.experiments", "gyrekit.runs.gridfile", "gyrekit.runs.read_field", "gyrekit.runs.read_spacing"):
    ex = Gr.experiments("R3"); yes("experiments found", len(ex) > 0); e0 = next(iter(ex.values())); yes("all file kinds", set(e0["files"]) == set(Gr.KINDS)); yes("no double slash", "//" not in e0["files"]["uvelfile"][0])
    yes("grid path", Gr.gridfile("R9").endswith("domain_cfg_R9.nc"))
    p = ncfile("g1.nc", dict(t=2, z=3, y=2, x=2), q=(("t", "z", "y", "x"), np.arange(24.).reshape(2, 3, 2, 2))); out = Gr.read_field([p, p], "q", levels=[1]); yes("concatenated and level picked", out.shape == (4, 1, 2, 2)); ok("value", out[0, 0, 0, 0] - 4, 0)
    p = ncfile("g2.nc", dict(t=1, y=2, x=2), e1t=(("t", "y", "x"), 5*np.ones((1, 2, 2))), e2t=(("t", "y", "x"), 7*np.ones((1, 2, 2)))); ok("spacing", np.array(Gr.read_spacing(p)) - [5, 7], 0)

py-kits › gyrekit › runs › read_field

read_field

Read a variable from several files, joined along time.

Description

$$X = \big[\, f_1[v];\ f_2[v];\ \dots \,\big] \text{ along time}$$

Syntax

field = read_field(paths, var)field = read_field(paths, var, levels=None, dtype='float32')

Input Arguments

paths — list
Files, in time order
var — str
Variable
levels — int — default None
Vertical levels of 4D fields, index or slice; None for all
dtype — str — default 'float32'
Type of the result

Output Arguments

field — float
Variable concatenated along its first axis

Example

p = ncfile("g1.nc", dict(t=2, z=3, y=2, x=2), q=(("t", "z", "y", "x"), np.arange(24.).reshape(2, 3, 2, 2))); out = Gr.read_field([p, p], "q", levels=[1]); yes("concatenated and level picked", out.shape == (4, 1, 2, 2)); ok("value", out[0, 0, 0, 0] - 4, 0)

py-kits › gyrekit › runs › read_spacing

read_spacing

The uniform grid spacing of a GYRE domain_cfg file.

Description

GYRE grids are regular, so the first cell's widths hold everywhere.

$$(\Delta x, \Delta y) = (e_{1t}, e_{2t})_{0,0}$$

Syntax

dx, dy = read_spacing(gridfile)

Input Arguments

gridfile — str
domain_cfg file

Output Arguments

dx — float
e1t at the first point, in metres
dy — float
e2t at the first point, in metres

Example

p = ncfile("g2.nc", dict(t=1, y=2, x=2), e1t=(("t", "y", "x"), 5*np.ones((1, 2, 2))), e2t=(("t", "y", "x"), 7*np.ones((1, 2, 2)))); ok("spacing", np.array(Gr.read_spacing(p)) - [5, 7], 0)
Whole test
